help.frlg-trade-host:--slot: 0-based host party slot offered for one trade (default: 1)
help.frlg-trade-host:--slots: comma-separated 0-based offered slots for multiple trades
help.frlg-trade-host:--union-room: host for the Union Room (the middle NPC on Pokemon Center 2F) instead of the trade centre's third NPC; use with --union-room-keepalive 120 and --board-type
help.frlg-trade-host:--colosseum: host the cable-club COLOSSEUM instead of the trade centre (Pokemon Center 2F, third NPC -> Colosseum -> Single Battle -> JOIN). The entry is the trade centre's, so --card-flag-id still arms the console's card counters, and only this path increments its battlesWon [decomp:src/cable_club.c:792]. The whole party fights
help.frlg-trade-host:--union-room-activity: which activity --union-room advertises; default 'in-room', the bare IN_UNION_ROOM a console standing in the room connects to. 'search' is what the screen before the room looks for (untested)
help.frlg-trade-host:--union-room-keepalive: Union Room: re-present a parent NI_START for N VBlanks before the first UNI frame; the room child drops the link after five unanswered frames, and enters UNI 480 frames after the last NI_START. 120 is proven
help.frlg-trade-host:--board-type: Union Room trading board: register the offered Pokemon (its species and level) and ask for this type in return, so the console's board lists us. The console must have a Pokemon of that type to start the trade
help.frlg-trade-host:--board-level: override the level shown on the trading board
help.frlg-trade-host:--union-room-chat: Union Room: accept the console's 'Tchat' instead of declining it. Both sides send a join block, then the console's keyboard opens and every line it types is logged
help.frlg-trade-host:--union-room-battle: Union Room: accept the console's Combat instead of declining it. The console needs two non-egg party mons at level 30 or lower or it refuses on its own screen; it is master and runs the battle, we answer its controller commands
help.frlg-trade-host:--battle-fight: Union Room battle: pick fight with the first move instead of forfeiting at the first action prompt. Only the forfeit path has been proven on hardware
help.frlg-trade-host:--battle-move: Union Room battle with --battle-fight: which of the active Pokemon's four move slots to use. The default 0 is whatever move slot one holds, which for the tracked party is refresh and does no damage
help.frlg-trade-host:--chat-file: Union Room chat: tail this file while the host runs and send every line appended to it, so the chat can be answered live instead of queued at launch
help.frlg-trade-host:--chat-message: Union Room chat: a line to send once the chat opens, repeatable. Up to 15 Gen-3 charmap characters each, the console's own keyboard limit and the width its chat line can draw; they go out one at a time, 1.5s apart
help.frlg-trade-host:--anim-delay: override the proven trade-animation frame delay
help.frlg-trade-host:--player-ids-repeat-fram: diagnostic: consecutive polls the opening SEND_PLAYER_IDS burst occupies before the LinkPlayer block request; default is the built-in timing
help.frlg-trade-host:--link-player-idle-frame: diagnostic: quiet console polls after the LinkPlayer exchange before the leader starts the trainer-card exchange itself
help.frlg-trade-host:--save-rounds: post-trade standby rounds before the parties are exchanged again; default 6, the Switch FireRed count. GBA Emerald runs 5 (docs/rse.md, After the trade)
help.frlg-trade-host:--online: trade with a player far away: their console's offer is offered here, and each side confirms only once both consoles have (docs/online.md)
help.frlg-trade-host:--online-code: the room both players enter; default the link code, and no code meets anyone else trading online without one
help.frlg-trade-host:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
help.frlg-trade-host:--print-effective-config: print the safe effective host configuration and exit
help.frlg-trade-host:--id: decimal trainer ID, optionally followed by decimal secret ID
help.frlg-trade-host:--card-flag-id: the Wonder Card flag id our trainer card claims in the Union Room card exchange. A console holding the card with that id arms its own card counters, so a trade or cable-club battle with us increments them [union_room.c:1777]; default 0, which arms nothing
help.frlg-trade-host:--no-trust-pia: use Pia-backed send-once block delivery (recommended); --no-trust-pia enables diagnostic RFU retransmits
help.frlg-trade-host:--verbose: show detailed protocol logging instead of milestones
help.frlg-trade-host:--password: LDN passphrase hex; default uses the frlg emulator value
help.frlg-trade-host:--adapter: named Wi-Fi adapter profile used while --phy is auto
help.frlg-trade-host:--over-ip: host for an emulated console over the LAN instead of over the radio: answer ldn_mitm discovery on port 11452 and carry Pia over UDP. Takes the address to advertise, or auto. Needs no adapter, no prod.keys and no root
help.frlg-trade-host:--capture: record an optional JSONL protocol diagnostic
help.frlg-trade-host:--scene: LDN scene; default is the known Direct Corner scene
help.frlg-trade-host:--no-skip-encryption: delegate transmit CCMP to mac80211/hardware; over-air frames remain encrypted
help.frlg-trade-host:--no-accept-decrypted-cc: accept hardware-decrypted RX frames that retain their CCMP header and mic (TP-Link Archer T3U/rtw88_8822bu profile)
help.frlg-trade-host:--no-native-nonce-sequen: use FireRed's session-wide incrementing Pia nonce
help.frlg-trade-host:--no-session-response-fi: send Session type 2 unicast before type 5 broadcast
help.frlg-trade-host:--tick-hz: how many RFU slots a second the host emits (default 59.727, one per GBA VBlank). A real console pair runs far below this; lowering it slows every link step by the same factor.
help.frlg-trade-join:--out: save the received mon here (trades=1); for trades>1 this is a base/prefix and each received mon is saved as <stem>_trade<k>_<species>.pk3
help.frlg-trade-join:--out-format: received mon format: pk3=decrypted (opens in PKHeX), ek3=encrypted/raw
help.frlg-trade-join:--slot: party slot to offer on the first round (default 1); the per-round default list grows ascending from here (or [0..N-1] for a full-party swap)
help.frlg-trade-join:--slots: explicit comma list of 0-based party slots to offer, one per trade (len must == --trades, distinct, each < party size), e.g. --slots 0,2,4
help.frlg-trade-join:--trades: number of sequential trades to perform, 1..6 (default 1; 6 = swap both entire parties). After the Nth trade the sim cancels-to-leave.
help.frlg-trade-join:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
help.frlg-trade-join:--self-id: wire mpId / gLocalLinkPlayerId (joiner = 1 = right seat; the only valid value - mpId 0 is the host/parent) [trade.c:1816; link_rfu_2.c:1633-1638]
help.frlg-trade-join:--id: decimal trainer ID, optionally followed by decimal secret ID
help.frlg-trade-join:--card-flag-id: the Wonder Card flag id our trainer card claims in the Union Room card exchange. A console holding the card with that id arms its own card counters, so a trade or cable-club battle with us increments them [union_room.c:1777]; default 0, which arms nothing
help.frlg-trade-join:--anim-delay: frames to wait after START_TRADE before READY_FINISH (default 1935, the wire-measured wireless DoTradeAnim duration)
help.frlg-trade-join:--decline: decline at the confirm prompt (confirm-NO -> immediate READY_CANCEL, graceful cancel-to-leave) [trade.c:2019-2023]
help.frlg-trade-join:--refuse-illegit: treat an offered Deoxys/Mew as PARTNER_MON_INVALID and cancel-to-leave (the host's illegitimate-legend gate; legitimacy is not offline-decodable) [trade.c:1965-1968]
help.frlg-trade-join:--no-trust-pia: send each block fragment once (fire-and-forget) instead of the console's re-send-until-confirmed loop. Default off (faithful re-send): against the real client, a block streams in 1-2s with aggressive re-sends (~1.5x) and completes; trust_pia's send-once crawled (~0.1 frag/s) and never completed. trust_pia was a workaround for the 'flood', but that was the rtt deadlock (now fixed). --trust-pia re-enables send-once
help.frlg-trade-join:--pace-ms: live: minimum ms between two datagrams to the console, merging what is due into one (0 = off). See sim.PACE_MIN_GAP_MS for the measurement.
help.frlg-trade-join:--connect-id: (live) override the RFU connection id (hex, e.g. 7036) sent in the emulator connect ('C') frame. Default: a random nonzero id - any nonzero value works. --parent-pid is a deprecated alias.
help.frlg-trade-join:--replay: offline: replay a capture's host stream
help.frlg-trade-join:--password: LDN passphrase as hex (live); default = the built-in 64-byte emulator passphrase (shared by frlg/rse)
help.frlg-trade-join:--phy: wifi phy for the LDN join (live)
help.frlg-trade-join:--keys: Switch prod.keys (live); default: keys_path from config/host*.toml
help.frlg-trade-join:--comm-id: LDN local_communication_id (hex) to join (live); if omitted, joins the only available network (scan logs candidates)
help.frlg-trade-join:--capture: (live) record every Pia datagram both directions to a .jsonl (incl. the SSID), so a live attempt can be decrypted/analysed offline

help.frlg-gift:--export-gift: save a .pokegift file and exit without using the radio
help.frlg-gift:--save-to-board: store the gift on the ESP32 board, which then hosts it for every console that joins, with no computer, at every power-up, and exit
help.frlg-gift:--save-backup: copy the console's whole 128 KB save into FILE (.sav); the console's save is not changed [docs/frlg_gift.md, Save backup and restore]
help.frlg-gift:--save-restore: write the .sav FILE onto the console: beside its newest save, every sector read back, then the game loads it and saves; anything short of that keeps the old save
help.frlg-gift:--save-resume-dir: with --save-backup: keep a backup the link cut short here; the next one goes on from it
help.frlg-gift:--news:
Wonder News payload to distribute (Mystery Gift -> Wonder News -> Friend).
Available news:
  pokeldn  id 1: the plain proof-of-link news, one berry from the man in CERULEAN CITY
  berry    id 2: a ten-line news that exercises the console's scroll indicator
help.frlg-gift:--buffer-script: run native ARM code on the console through CLI_RUN_BUFFER_SCRIPT instead of sending a gift: trainer-id-probe: read playerTrainerId out of gSaveBlock2Ptr and return it (reads only, writes nothing); save-dump: read out any part of either save block, using the pointers the console hands us - no absolute address needed (reads only, writes nothing); memory-dump: read out any region of the console's memory by repointing the console's own outgoing message at it (needs --dump-address; reads only, writes nothing); memory-dump-multi: the same, but SEVERAL consecutive blocks in one session (--dump-address --dump-blocks N): the client script runs the payload once per block and each pass sends the next kilobyte; memory-dump-scatter: the same, but the blocks are UNRELATED addresses (--dump-scatter A,B,C): the payload carries a table of bases and the cursor indexes it, so one session reads the sixteen kilobytes a plan actually asked for rather than sixteen consecutive ones; save-write: write bytes into a save block and read the same region back in the same run; the console saves afterwards, so the write reaches flash (--write-hex, --dump-block, --dump-offset); rng-trace: sample one word of memory once a frame, optionally calling a ROM function between the two halves of each sample, and check the LCG recurrence on what comes back (--trace-address, --trace-call, --trace-samples; reads only, plus whatever the callee does); memory-scan: search memory for a 32-bit value and send back where it is; it returns 0 to be called again next frame, so one run covers a range no dump could (--scan-word, --scan-start, --scan-end, --scan-blocks; reads only, writes nothing); table-scan: search memory for a table by its shape, a run of N words each exactly D above the one before it, and send back where each run starts and what value it starts with; this is how a table of pointers is found when no constant in it is known (--table-delta, --table-runlen, --table-start, --table-end, --table-blocks; reads only, writes nothing); rom-checksum: checksum a range of memory in up to 128 blocks and send back one sum per block; the host sets them beside the same sums over a ROM image and names the blocks that differ (--sum-start, --sum-end, --sum-block, --sum-budget, --sum-reference; reads only, writes nothing); anchors: ask the machine where it is: our own load address, the return address into ROM, the stack and the client's five buffers (writes only its own outgoing buffer); create-mon: call CreateMon, a ROM function taking eight arguments, and send back the 100-byte struct Pokemon it built; the mon is built inside our own image, so nothing on the console is written unless --create-mon-append or --create-mon-destination asks for it (--create-mon-call, --create-mon-species, --create-mon-level, --create-mon-personality); string-gather: follow an array of pointers and send back the strings themselves, back to back, instead of a window of mostly-pointers: a whole Easy Chat group in one run (--gather-address, --gather-count, --gather-stride; reads only, writes nothing); call: call any ROM function with arguments we choose, up to eight words in r0..r3 then the stack, and send back its r0 with one address read either side of the call (--call-address, --call-arg, --call-watch); the payload writes nothing itself, but the callee may, so the address has to have been read as code first; flash-read: select the flash bank, byte-copy a save sector out of the 64 KiB window into EWRAM with the CPU, and send the COPY: the console's outgoing message cannot be pointed at flash itself (--flash-sector, --flash-read-offset, --dump-size; reads only, writes nothing); flash-patch: read a save sector out of flash through the banked window, change one field, recompute the checksum and write it back with swi 0x48, then bump the counter-bearing sector so the loader adopts the band. Nothing is rebuilt from RAM, so a field the save routine serializes cannot be lost (--flash-id, --flash-patch-offset, --flash-patch-hex; needs --write-unsafe); flash-write: compose 4 KB in EWRAM on the console and write it straight into a flash sector with swi 0x48, instead of going through the game's save code entirely - no counter, checksum or signature (--flash-sector, --flash-fill-base, --flash-fill-step, --flash-words; a sector inside the save bands needs --write-unsafe); call-chain: run a LIST of ROM calls and memory accesses in one frame and send back a word for each, any step able to use the previous step's result as its address - which is how a function that returns a pointer (GetVarPointer) becomes a write (--chain-step, repeatable; a write step needs --write-unsafe); sloop-svc: issue one Sloop syscall (swi 0x40..0x62) with r0..r3 we choose, optionally pointing r0 or r1 at up to 256 bytes we send, and send back the registers and the bytes as the syscall left them (--svc-number, --svc-arg, --svc-text/--svc-hex, --svc-data-in; a number outside the read-only set needs --write-unsafe); install-resident: copy a resident hook into the top of EWRAM and install it in gIntrTable[4], where it runs every frame until a soft reset; answers with the V-blank handler it found (--resident turbo, --resident-param extra=N field=N battle=N hold=0x100 budget=228; needs --write-unsafe); install-kept: install the resident hook kept in the save's filler_B20 (written by save-write --resident), after checking its sum; answers with the V-blank handler it found, 0xBAD0BAD0 when nothing was installed
help.frlg-gift:--dump-address: with --buffer-script memory-dump: the console address to read out (0x02000000 EWRAM, 0x03000000 IWRAM, 0x08000000 ROM). Accepts 0x hex
help.frlg-gift:--dump-scatter: with --buffer-script memory-dump-scatter: the UNRELATED addresses to read, one block each, in this order. A plan asks for scattered kilobytes rather than one long region, and this is the payload that answers it. Accepts 0x hex
help.frlg-gift:--dump-blocks: with --buffer-script memory-dump-multi: how many consecutive blocks to pull in ONE session. MG_LINK_BUFFER_SIZE caps a message, not a session, so the client script runs the payload once per block and each pass sends the next one
help.frlg-gift:--dump-size: with --buffer-script memory-dump: how many bytes to read, 1..1024 (MG_LINK_BUFFER_SIZE)
help.frlg-gift:--dump-block: with --buffer-script save-dump: which save block to read; sav2 is name, trainer id and pokedex, sav1 is party, bag, money, flags and vars
help.frlg-gift:--dump-offset: with --buffer-script save-dump: byte offset into that block. Accepts 0x hex
help.frlg-gift:--dump-file: with a dumping --buffer-script: write the bytes that come back to this file
help.frlg-gift:--table-delta: with --buffer-script table-scan: what each word of the run must exceed the one before it by. 2 finds a table of pointers to consecutive u16s, which is what gSpecialVars is. Accepts 0x hex
help.frlg-gift:--table-runlen: with --buffer-script table-scan: how many words in a row make a run worth reporting (default 12, the twelve gSpecialVar_0x8000..0x800B entries)
help.frlg-gift:--table-start: with --buffer-script table-scan: where to start, 16-byte aligned (default 0x08000000, the cartridge)
help.frlg-gift:--table-end: with --buffer-script table-scan: one past the last address to read (default 0x09000000)
help.frlg-gift:--table-blocks: with --buffer-script table-scan: 16-byte blocks scanned per frame (default 192, the same instruction load on the frame that memory-scan's 512 costs)
help.frlg-gift:--table-max-calls: with --buffer-script table-scan: the watchdog, in calls (= frames)
help.frlg-gift:--sum-start: with --buffer-script rom-checksum: where to start, aligned to --sum-block (default 0x08000000, the cartridge)
help.frlg-gift:--sum-end: with --buffer-script rom-checksum: one past the last address to sum, a whole number of blocks after --sum-start (default 0x09000000)
help.frlg-gift:--sum-block: with --buffer-script rom-checksum: the block size, a power of two from 32; the range holds at most 128 blocks (default 0x20000)
help.frlg-gift:--sum-budget: with --buffer-script rom-checksum: 32-byte chunks summed per frame (default 512, no more load on the frame than memory-scan's 512)
help.frlg-gift:--sum-max-calls: with --buffer-script rom-checksum: the watchdog, in calls (= frames) (default: what the range needs, plus two)
help.frlg-gift:--sum-reference: with --buffer-script rom-checksum: the ROM image to compare the sums with (default: the image config.REFERENCE_ROMS names for the console's build)
help.frlg-gift:--scan-word: with --buffer-script memory-scan: the 32-bit value to search for. The payload returns 0 to be called again next frame, so one run scans a whole range instead of the 1024 bytes a dump reads. Accepts 0x hex
help.frlg-gift:--scan-start: with --buffer-script memory-scan: where to start, 32-byte aligned (default 0x08000000, the cartridge)
help.frlg-gift:--scan-end: with --buffer-script memory-scan: one past the last address to read (default 0x09000000, the end of a 16 MB cartridge)
help.frlg-gift:--scan-blocks: with --buffer-script memory-scan: 32-byte blocks scanned per frame, the budget the console's link has to live with (default 512, about 3 ms of a 16 ms frame)
help.frlg-gift:--scan-max-calls: with --buffer-script memory-scan: the watchdog. A payload that never returns 1 hangs the Mystery Gift menu, so the scan gives up and answers after this many frames (default: what the range needs, plus two)
help.frlg-gift:--gather-address: with --buffer-script string-gather: the address of the first pointer in an array to follow. The answer is the strings themselves, back to back, so one run carries a whole table instead of a window of mostly-pointers. Accepts 0x hex
help.frlg-gift:--gather-count: with --buffer-script string-gather: how many pointers to follow at most
help.frlg-gift:--gather-stride: with --buffer-script string-gather: bytes from one pointer to the next (default 12, struct EasyChatWordInfo, whose `text` is at offset 0; a plain array of `const u8 *` is 4)
help.frlg-gift:--gather-maxlen: with --buffer-script string-gather: longest string accepted, terminator included. A pointer that is not a string would otherwise be copied until it met an 0xFF (default 64)
help.frlg-gift:--trace-address: with --buffer-script rng-trace: the word to sample once a frame. gRngValue is 0x03004220 on the French cartridges and 0x030042D0 on the English ones [builds.py]. Accepts 0x hex
help.frlg-gift:--trace-call: with --buffer-script rng-trace: a ROM function to call between the two reads of each sample, as a THUMB pointer (bit 0 set), or 0 for none. Random is 0x080486B1 French, 0x08048671 English; the recurrence between the two reads is then the proof that both addresses are what we say they are
help.frlg-gift:--trace-samples: with --buffer-script rng-trace: how many frames to sample, 1..96
help.frlg-gift:--call-address: with --buffer-script call: the ROM function to call, as a THUMB pointer (bit 0 set). SeedRng is 0x080486D1 and Random 0x080486B1 on the French cartridges, 0x08048691 and 0x08048671 on the English ones [builds.py]. The address is sent as given, so pair it with --console-build. 0 calls nothing, which checks the send path with the ROM left out
help.frlg-gift:--call-arg: with --buffer-script call: one argument word, repeatable, up to eight. The first four go in r0..r3 and the rest on the stack at [sp+0..12], where CreateMon's own prologue reads them
help.frlg-gift:--call-watch: with --buffer-script call: one word read immediately before and immediately after the call, both returned. gRngValue is 0x03004220 French, 0x030042D0 English. For a function that returns nothing, such as SeedRng, this is the only evidence the call did what it was called for
help.frlg-gift:--expect-console: refuse the session unless the console that joins is this cartridge, checked against the version in its game data. Nothing is sent on a mismatch
help.frlg-gift:--console-build: whose addresses a hook, a stub or a ROM call is built with: BPRF, BPGF, BPRE, BPGE, BPRS, BPGS, BPRD, BPGD, BPRI, BPGI, BPRJ, BPGJ. auto (the default) builds for each and sends the one the console's game code names, before anything address-dependent is sent; another code is refused. A game code serves only that cartridge. Bytes with no build address go to any console either way
help.frlg-gift:--chain-step: with --buffer-script call-chain: one step, repeatable, up to 16, run in order in one frame. `call:NAME_OR_ADDR[,ARG]...` calls a ROM function (AddBagItem, AddMoney, AddPCItem, CalcCRC16, CheckBagHasItem, CheckBagHasSpace, CompactPartySlots, CreateMon, FlagClear, FlagGet, FlagSet, GetMoney, GetSetPokedexFlag, GetVarPointer, IncrementGameStat, InitRamScript, IsEnoughMoney, ItemIsMail, Random, ReadFlash, RemoveBagItem, RemoveMoney, RunScriptImmediately, SeedRng, SpeciesToNationalPokedexNum, StringCompare, VarGet, VarSet, or a THUMB address); `read32|read16|read8:ADDR` reads; `write32|write16|write8:ADDR,VALUE` writes and reads itself back, and needs --write-unsafe. A target of `prev` is the PREVIOUS step's result and `prev+N` is N bytes past it, which is how a function that returns a pointer becomes a write; an op may carry +keep to leave prev alone. Example: --chain-step call:GetVarPointer,0x4024 --chain-step write16:prev,7. A named function is resolved on the console's build
help.frlg-gift:--create-mon-call: with --buffer-script create-mon: the ROM function to call with eight arguments, a THUMB pointer. The default is the console build's CreateMon (0x08041151 French, 0x080411FD English); 0 calls nothing, which checks the send path with the ROM left out
help.frlg-gift:--create-mon-species: with --buffer-script create-mon: the species number, 1..411 (internal numbering, not the National Dex)
help.frlg-gift:--create-mon-iv: with --buffer-script create-mon: every IV set to this, 0..31. 32 or more rolls them instead [USE_RANDOM_IVS], which makes the run non-deterministic
help.frlg-gift:--create-mon-personality: with --buffer-script create-mon: the 32-bit personality value, which fixes the nature, the gender, the ability slot and, with the trainer ids, whether the mon is shiny. Omitted, the console rolls one with Random32
help.frlg-gift:--create-mon-ot-id-type: with --buffer-script create-mon: 0 = the OT is the player and the id comes off the real save, 1 = use --create-mon-ot-id, 2 = rolled until not shiny
help.frlg-gift:--create-mon-ot-id: with --buffer-script create-mon --create-mon-ot-id-type 1: the OT id to use
help.frlg-gift:--create-mon-append: with --buffer-script create-mon: append the finished mon to the player's party. The slot is computed from gSaveBlock1Ptr, never given, and it is always the first free one - playerParty[playerPartyCount] - so an occupied slot is never touched and no Pokemon can be destroyed. A full party writes nothing and says so. This is the player's live SAVE and the console commits it to flash: needs --write-unsafe
help.frlg-gift:--create-mon-append-dry-run: with --buffer-script create-mon: the same run as --create-mon-append - the same call, the same arithmetic on the same gSaveBlock1Ptr - with the two stores that would change the save left out. It reports the party count and the address it would have written, and reads that slot's current 100 bytes back so the answer says what a real run would overwrite. Writes nothing, so it needs no override
help.frlg-gift:--create-mon-destination: with --buffer-script create-mon: copy the finished 100 bytes to this address in the console's memory. The mon is built in our own image either way, so without this nothing on the console is written at all. Needs --write-unsafe
help.frlg-gift:--write-text: with --buffer-script save-write: ascii to write into the save block at --dump-offset. The same region is read back in the same run, so the answer is the proof. The console saves afterwards, so it reaches flash
help.frlg-gift:--write-hex: with --buffer-script save-write: the bytes to write, as hex
help.frlg-gift:--flash-sector: with --buffer-script flash-write: the 4 KB flash sector (0..31) swi 0x48 writes. Sectors 0..27 are the two save bands and need --write-unsafe; 28..31 are outside both
help.frlg-gift:--flash-fill-base: with --buffer-script flash-write: word[0] of the pattern the console composes
help.frlg-gift:--flash-fill-step: with --buffer-script flash-write: added to each word of the pattern
help.frlg-gift:--flash-words: with --buffer-script flash-write: how many words of the sector to compose
help.frlg-gift:--flash-footer: with --buffer-script flash-write: compose a WELL-FORMED save sector instead of a raw pattern - the console zeroes past the data, computes the game's own checksum over the 3968-byte data area and lays down id, checksum, signature and counter
help.frlg-gift:--flash-id: with --flash-footer: the sector id written at +0xFF4
help.frlg-gift:--flash-counter: with --flash-footer: the save counter written at +0xFFC
help.frlg-gift:--flash-derive: with --flash-footer: read gLastWrittenSector and gSaveCounter on the console and write the sector the --flash-id actually occupies right now, rather than a position computed when the payload was built. Needs --write-unsafe
help.frlg-gift:--svc-number: with --buffer-script sloop-svc: a syscall, 0x40..0x62 (0x4D is the bad-word check); repeat for up to eight, issued in order in one session
help.frlg-gift:--svc-arg: with --buffer-script sloop-svc: r0, r1, r2, r3 in order (repeatable)
help.frlg-gift:--svc-text: with --buffer-script sloop-svc: up to 256 bytes of UTF-8 data to send
help.frlg-gift:--svc-hex: with --buffer-script sloop-svc: the data as hex instead
help.frlg-gift:--resident: with --buffer-script install-resident: the hook to install (turbo)
help.frlg-gift:--resident-param: with --buffer-script install-resident: a hook parameter, e.g. extra=6
help.frlg-gift:--svc-bkpt: with --buffer-script sloop-svc: issue THUMB `bkpt N` instead of `swi N` (0xFF is the one the game never issues; needs --write-unsafe)
help.frlg-gift:--svc-data-in: with --buffer-script sloop-svc: point this register at the console's copy of the data
help.frlg-gift:--flash-read-offset: with --buffer-script flash-read: byte offset into the sector to start reading at
help.frlg-gift:--flash-patch-offset: with --buffer-script flash-patch: byte offset of the field inside the sector's data
help.frlg-gift:--flash-patch-hex: with --buffer-script flash-patch: the replacement bytes for that field, as hex. Everything else in the sector is whatever the game's own save routine wrote
help.frlg-gift:--flash-position: with --flash-derive: aim at band position N (0..13) and derive the ID from it, instead of deriving the position from --flash-id. Position 13 is the sector whose counter GetSaveValidStatus reports for the whole slot
help.frlg-gift:--flash-counter-bias: with --flash-derive: added to gSaveCounter for the footer. 0 keeps the sector in its own band; a positive value is what would outrank the live slot
help.frlg-gift:--write-unsafe: allow a save write outside struct SaveBlock2's never-read filler regions. This is the player's live save and the console commits it to flash; without this the write is refused
help.frlg-gift:--flag-id: Wonder Card flagId, 1000..1019; without this option, the selected gift's registered default shown below is used
help.frlg-gift:--questionnaire:
require the console to be holding this four-word Easy Chat phrase in its Poke Mart
questionnaire before anything is sent [SVR_CHECK_QUESTIONNAIRE]. Each word is an
English word name, `species:N`, `move:N`, `group/index`, or a raw id. Word ids are
per-language outside the species and move groups, so read the phrase off the target
console first: every session logs the four ids it is holding.
help.frlg-gift:--denied-message: what a console that does not know the phrase reads (max 63 characters); the default is 'That is not the phrase.'
help.frlg-gift:--hunt-nature:
with --gift rng-mon-hunt: which natures the search will accept, comma separated
(Hardy, Lonely, Brave, Adamant, Naughty, Bold, ...), or plain ids. Without this it takes any.
help.frlg-gift:--hunt-iv:
with --gift rng-mon-hunt: a floor under one IV, repeatable (speed=31, attack=20). The stats
are hp, attack, defense, speed, sp_attack, sp_defense, named in the order the ROM draws them - which is not the order the summary
screen shows.
help.frlg-gift:--event-pokemon:
with --gift event-pokemon: a fresh copy of a Gen 3 distribution, made by PKHeX by that event's
own PID/IV method, e.g. "WISHMKR Jirachi", "10 ANIV Pikachu", "Aura Mew". The
release in --language is preferred. Without it the card sends a stored WISHMKR Jirachi.
help.frlg-gift:--hunt-cap:
with --gift rng-mon-hunt: how many states the stub may try before giving up and leaving the
rng alone. The default is the smallest cap that finds one 99 times in 100.
help.frlg-gift:--hunt-species:
with --gift rng-mon-hunt: what the stub's own `setwildbattle` puts on the screen. Neither the
species nor the level is drawn from the rng, so this changes nothing about the
search. The default is a level 5 MAGIKARP, which is catchable in one ball.
help.frlg-gift:--hunt-level: with --gift rng-mon-hunt: the level that species appears at.
help.frlg-gift:--ram-script-map-group:
which map group the RAM script binds to (a group_order index in
[decomp:data/maps/map_groups.json]). The default is the player's house, where the
mother never moves. Cerulean Cave B1F is group 1 map 74, and MEWTWO is object 3.
help.frlg-gift:--ram-script-map-num: which map in that group the RAM script binds to.
help.frlg-gift:--ram-script-object:
which object event on that map. Local ids are assigned in map.json order and start
at 1. Binding REPLACES that object's own script, so choose one that never moves.
help.frlg-gift:--hunt-freeze-frames:
with --gift rng-mon-hunt: how long the search may block the overworld in the worst case,
in frames (default 900, about 15 s). The field engine has not returned while it
searches, so the player sees a still frame with the music playing; criteria whose
search could take longer than this are refused before the card is built.
help.frlg-gift:--news-id: override the news id (1..65535). A console keeps news only when it differs from what it already holds [IsWonderNewsSameAsSaved], so bump this to re-send the same text to the same console
help.frlg-gift:--client-ready-idle-frames: diagnostic: quiet child polls after LinkPlayer standby before the first Mystery Gift message; default is the built-in timing
help.frlg-gift:--inter-block-gap-frames: diagnostic: idle VBlanks between the blocks of one Mystery Gift message; raise it if a run stalls part-way through a message (default is the built-in timing)
help.frlg-gift:--block-repeat: emit each block fragment N times (1-8, default 2); bounded redundancy against the console's silent datagram drops
help.frlg-gift:--ram-script-block-repeat: fragment redundancy for the ident-25 delivery script alone (1-8, default 3); the console never reflects gift blocks, so a lost fragment cannot be resent
help.frlg-gift:--no-end-on-success: stop after the post-delivery RFU close sequence; used by the supervised run_mystery_gift.sh host
help.frlg-gift:--idle-timeout: stop after this many seconds without meaningful Switch traffic (join or Pia/RFU datagram); default: disabled
help.frlg-gift:--attempt-log-dir: append completed joined-attempt records to daily csv files in DIR; default: disabled (the supervised shell host enables logs/)
help.frlg-gift:--game-data-log: append what the console says about itself - its card counters, its four questionnaire words and its Easy Chat battle profile - to this jsonl ledger. tools/frlg/game_data_read.py reads it back and says what moved between sessions
help.frlg-gift:--no-make-artifact: write an annotated listing for the exact Mystery Gift bytes that will be sent (default: disabled)

help.rse-trade-host:--slots: comma-separated 0-based offered slots for multiple trades
help.rse-trade-host:--union-room: host for the Union Room (the middle NPC on Pokemon Center 2F) instead of the trade centre's third NPC; use with --union-room-keepalive 120 and --board-type
help.rse-trade-host:--colosseum: host the cable-club COLOSSEUM instead of the trade centre (Pokemon Center 2F, third NPC -> Colosseum -> Single Battle -> JOIN). The entry is the trade centre's, so --card-flag-id still arms the console's card counters, and only this path increments its battlesWon [decomp:src/cable_club.c:792]. The whole party fights
help.rse-trade-host:--union-room-activity: which activity --union-room advertises; default 'in-room', the bare IN_UNION_ROOM a console standing in the room connects to. 'search' is what the screen before the room looks for (untested)
help.rse-trade-host:--union-room-keepalive: Union Room: re-present a parent NI_START for N VBlanks before the first UNI frame; the room child drops the link after five unanswered frames, and enters UNI 480 frames after the last NI_START. 120 is proven
help.rse-trade-host:--board-type: Union Room trading board: register the offered Pokemon (its species and level) and ask for this type in return, so the console's board lists us. The console must have a Pokemon of that type to start the trade
help.rse-trade-host:--board-level: override the level shown on the trading board
help.rse-trade-host:--union-room-chat: Union Room: accept the console's 'Tchat' instead of declining it. Both sides send a join block, then the console's keyboard opens and every line it types is logged
help.rse-trade-host:--union-room-battle: Union Room: accept the console's Combat instead of declining it. The console needs two non-egg party mons at level 30 or lower or it refuses on its own screen; it is master and runs the battle, we answer its controller commands
help.rse-trade-host:--battle-fight: Union Room battle: pick fight with the first move instead of forfeiting at the first action prompt. Only the forfeit path has been proven on hardware
help.rse-trade-host:--battle-move: Union Room battle with --battle-fight: which of the active Pokemon's four move slots to use. The default 0 is whatever move slot one holds, which for the tracked party is refresh and does no damage
help.rse-trade-host:--chat-file: Union Room chat: tail this file while the host runs and send every line appended to it, so the chat can be answered live instead of queued at launch
help.rse-trade-host:--chat-message: Union Room chat: a line to send once the chat opens, repeatable. Up to 15 Gen-3 charmap characters each, the console's own keyboard limit and the width its chat line can draw; they go out one at a time, 1.5s apart

help.rse-trade-host:--link-player-idle-frames: diagnostic: quiet console polls after the LinkPlayer exchange before the leader starts the trainer-card exchange itself
help.rse-trade-host:--save-rounds: post-trade standby rounds before the parties are exchanged again; default 6, the Switch FireRed count. GBA Emerald runs 5 (docs/rse.md, After the trade)
help.rse-trade-host:--online: trade with a player far away: their console's offer is offered here, and each side confirms only once both consoles have (docs/online.md)
help.rse-trade-host:--online-code: the room both players enter; default the link code, and no code meets anyone else trading online without one

help.rse-gift:--save-to-board: store the gift on the ESP32 board, which then hosts it for every console that joins, with no computer, at every power-up, and exit
help.rse-gift:--save-backup: copy the console's whole 128 KB save into FILE (.sav); the console's save is not changed [docs/frlg_gift.md, Save backup and restore]
help.rse-gift:--save-restore: write the .sav FILE onto the console: beside its newest save, every sector read back, then the game loads it and saves; anything short of that keeps the old save
help.rse-gift:--save-resume-dir: with --save-backup: keep a backup the link cut short here; the next one goes on from it
help.rse-gift:--news:
Wonder News payload to distribute (Mystery Gift -> Wonder News -> Friend).
Available news:
  pokeldn  id 1: the plain proof-of-link news, one berry from the man in CERULEAN CITY
  berry    id 2: a ten-line news that exercises the console's scroll indicator
help.rse-gift:--buffer-script: run native ARM code on the console through CLI_RUN_BUFFER_SCRIPT instead of sending a gift: trainer-id-probe: read playerTrainerId out of gSaveBlock2Ptr and return it (reads only, writes nothing); save-dump: read out any part of either save block, using the pointers the console hands us - no absolute address needed (reads only, writes nothing); memory-dump: read out any region of the console's memory by repointing the console's own outgoing message at it (needs --dump-address; reads only, writes nothing); memory-dump-multi: the same, but SEVERAL consecutive blocks in one session (--dump-address --dump-blocks N): the client script runs the payload once per block and each pass sends the next kilobyte; memory-dump-scatter: the same, but the blocks are UNRELATED addresses (--dump-scatter A,B,C): the payload carries a table of bases and the cursor indexes it, so one session reads the sixteen kilobytes a plan actually asked for rather than sixteen consecutive ones; save-write: write bytes into a save block and read the same region back in the same run; the console saves afterwards, so the write reaches flash (--write-hex, --dump-block, --dump-offset); rng-trace: sample one word of memory once a frame, optionally calling a ROM function between the two halves of each sample, and check the LCG recurrence on what comes back (--trace-address, --trace-call, --trace-samples; reads only, plus whatever the callee does); memory-scan: search memory for a 32-bit value and send back where it is; it returns 0 to be called again next frame, so one run covers a range no dump could (--scan-word, --scan-start, --scan-end, --scan-blocks; reads only, writes nothing); table-scan: search memory for a table by its shape, a run of N words each exactly D above the one before it, and send back where each run starts and what value it starts with; this is how a table of pointers is found when no constant in it is known (--table-delta, --table-runlen, --table-start, --table-end, --table-blocks; reads only, writes nothing); rom-checksum: checksum a range of memory in up to 128 blocks and send back one sum per block; the host sets them beside the same sums over a ROM image and names the blocks that differ (--sum-start, --sum-end, --sum-block, --sum-budget, --sum-reference; reads only, writes nothing); anchors: ask the machine where it is: our own load address, the return address into ROM, the stack and the client's five buffers (writes only its own outgoing buffer); create-mon: call CreateMon, a ROM function taking eight arguments, and send back the 100-byte struct Pokemon it built; the mon is built inside our own image, so nothing on the console is written unless --create-mon-append or --create-mon-destination asks for it (--create-mon-call, --create-mon-species, --create-mon-level, --create-mon-personality); string-gather: follow an array of pointers and send back the strings themselves, back to back, instead of a window of mostly-pointers: a whole Easy Chat group in one run (--gather-address, --gather-count, --gather-stride; reads only, writes nothing); call: call any ROM function with arguments we choose, up to eight words in r0..r3 then the stack, and send back its r0 with one address read either side of the call (--call-address, --call-arg, --call-watch); the payload writes nothing itself, but the callee may, so the address has to have been read as code first; flash-read: select the flash bank, byte-copy a save sector out of the 64 KiB window into EWRAM with the CPU, and send the COPY: the console's outgoing message cannot be pointed at flash itself (--flash-sector, --flash-read-offset, --dump-size; reads only, writes nothing); flash-patch: read a save sector out of flash through the banked window, change one field, recompute the checksum and write it back with swi 0x48, then bump the counter-bearing sector so the loader adopts the band. Nothing is rebuilt from RAM, so a field the save routine serializes cannot be lost (--flash-id, --flash-patch-offset, --flash-patch-hex; needs --write-unsafe); flash-write: compose 4 KB in EWRAM on the console and write it straight into a flash sector with swi 0x48, instead of going through the game's save code entirely - no counter, checksum or signature (--flash-sector, --flash-fill-base, --flash-fill-step, --flash-words; a sector inside the save bands needs --write-unsafe); call-chain: run a LIST of ROM calls and memory accesses in one frame and send back a word for each, any step able to use the previous step's result as its address - which is how a function that returns a pointer (GetVarPointer) becomes a write (--chain-step, repeatable; a write step needs --write-unsafe); sloop-svc: issue one Sloop syscall (swi 0x40..0x62) with r0..r3 we choose, optionally pointing r0 or r1 at up to 256 bytes we send, and send back the registers and the bytes as the syscall left them (--svc-number, --svc-arg, --svc-text/--svc-hex, --svc-data-in; a number outside the read-only set needs --write-unsafe); install-resident: copy a resident hook into the top of EWRAM and install it in gIntrTable[4], where it runs every frame until a soft reset; answers with the V-blank handler it found (--resident turbo, --resident-param extra=N field=N battle=N hold=0x100 budget=228; needs --write-unsafe); install-kept: install the resident hook kept in the save's filler_B20 (written by save-write --resident), after checking its sum; answers with the V-blank handler it found, 0xBAD0BAD0 when nothing was installed
help.rse-gift:--dump-address: with --buffer-script memory-dump: the console address to read out (0x02000000 EWRAM, 0x03000000 IWRAM, 0x08000000 ROM). Accepts 0x hex
help.rse-gift:--dump-scatter: with --buffer-script memory-dump-scatter: the UNRELATED addresses to read, one block each, in this order. A plan asks for scattered kilobytes rather than one long region, and this is the payload that answers it. Accepts 0x hex
help.rse-gift:--dump-blocks: with --buffer-script memory-dump-multi: how many consecutive blocks to pull in ONE session. MG_LINK_BUFFER_SIZE caps a message, not a session, so the client script runs the payload once per block and each pass sends the next one
help.rse-gift:--dump-size: with --buffer-script memory-dump: how many bytes to read, 1..1024 (MG_LINK_BUFFER_SIZE)
help.rse-gift:--dump-block: with --buffer-script save-dump: which save block to read; sav2 is name, trainer id and pokedex, sav1 is party, bag, money, flags and vars
help.rse-gift:--dump-offset: with --buffer-script save-dump: byte offset into that block. Accepts 0x hex
help.rse-gift:--dump-file: with a dumping --buffer-script: write the bytes that come back to this file
help.rse-gift:--table-delta: with --buffer-script table-scan: what each word of the run must exceed the one before it by. 2 finds a table of pointers to consecutive u16s, which is what gSpecialVars is. Accepts 0x hex
help.rse-gift:--table-runlen: with --buffer-script table-scan: how many words in a row make a run worth reporting (default 12, the twelve gSpecialVar_0x8000..0x800B entries)
help.rse-gift:--table-start: with --buffer-script table-scan: where to start, 16-byte aligned (default 0x08000000, the cartridge)
help.rse-gift:--table-end: with --buffer-script table-scan: one past the last address to read (default 0x09000000)
help.rse-gift:--table-blocks: with --buffer-script table-scan: 16-byte blocks scanned per frame (default 192, the same instruction load on the frame that memory-scan's 512 costs)
help.rse-gift:--table-max-calls: with --buffer-script table-scan: the watchdog, in calls (= frames)
help.rse-gift:--sum-start: with --buffer-script rom-checksum: where to start, aligned to --sum-block (default 0x08000000, the cartridge)
help.rse-gift:--sum-end: with --buffer-script rom-checksum: one past the last address to sum, a whole number of blocks after --sum-start (default 0x09000000)
help.rse-gift:--sum-block: with --buffer-script rom-checksum: the block size, a power of two from 32; the range holds at most 128 blocks (default 0x20000)
help.rse-gift:--sum-budget: with --buffer-script rom-checksum: 32-byte chunks summed per frame (default 512, no more load on the frame than memory-scan's 512)
help.rse-gift:--sum-max-calls: with --buffer-script rom-checksum: the watchdog, in calls (= frames) (default: what the range needs, plus two)
help.rse-gift:--sum-reference: with --buffer-script rom-checksum: the ROM image to compare the sums with (default: the image config.REFERENCE_ROMS names for the console's build)
help.rse-gift:--scan-word: with --buffer-script memory-scan: the 32-bit value to search for. The payload returns 0 to be called again next frame, so one run scans a whole range instead of the 1024 bytes a dump reads. Accepts 0x hex
help.rse-gift:--scan-start: with --buffer-script memory-scan: where to start, 32-byte aligned (default 0x08000000, the cartridge)
help.rse-gift:--scan-end: with --buffer-script memory-scan: one past the last address to read (default 0x09000000, the end of a 16 MB cartridge)
help.rse-gift:--scan-blocks: with --buffer-script memory-scan: 32-byte blocks scanned per frame, the budget the console's link has to live with (default 512, about 3 ms of a 16 ms frame)
help.rse-gift:--scan-max-calls: with --buffer-script memory-scan: the watchdog. A payload that never returns 1 hangs the Mystery Gift menu, so the scan gives up and answers after this many frames (default: what the range needs, plus two)
help.rse-gift:--gather-address: with --buffer-script string-gather: the address of the first pointer in an array to follow. The answer is the strings themselves, back to back, so one run carries a whole table instead of a window of mostly-pointers. Accepts 0x hex
help.rse-gift:--gather-count: with --buffer-script string-gather: how many pointers to follow at most
help.rse-gift:--gather-stride: with --buffer-script string-gather: bytes from one pointer to the next (default 12, struct EasyChatWordInfo, whose `text` is at offset 0; a plain array of `const u8 *` is 4)
help.rse-gift:--gather-maxlen: with --buffer-script string-gather: longest string accepted, terminator included. A pointer that is not a string would otherwise be copied until it met an 0xFF (default 64)
help.rse-gift:--trace-address: with --buffer-script rng-trace: the word to sample once a frame. gRngValue is 0x03004220 on the French cartridges and 0x030042D0 on the English ones [builds.py]. Accepts 0x hex
help.rse-gift:--trace-call: with --buffer-script rng-trace: a ROM function to call between the two reads of each sample, as a THUMB pointer (bit 0 set), or 0 for none. Random is 0x080486B1 French, 0x08048671 English; the recurrence between the two reads is then the proof that both addresses are what we say they are
help.rse-gift:--trace-samples: with --buffer-script rng-trace: how many frames to sample, 1..96
help.rse-gift:--call-address: with --buffer-script call: the ROM function to call, as a THUMB pointer (bit 0 set). SeedRng is 0x080486D1 and Random 0x080486B1 on the French cartridges, 0x08048691 and 0x08048671 on the English ones [builds.py]. The address is sent as given, so pair it with --console-build. 0 calls nothing, which checks the send path with the ROM left out
help.rse-gift:--call-arg: with --buffer-script call: one argument word, repeatable, up to eight. The first four go in r0..r3 and the rest on the stack at [sp+0..12], where CreateMon's own prologue reads them
help.rse-gift:--call-watch: with --buffer-script call: one word read immediately before and immediately after the call, both returned. gRngValue is 0x03004220 French, 0x030042D0 English. For a function that returns nothing, such as SeedRng, this is the only evidence the call did what it was called for
help.rse-gift:--expect-console: refuse the session unless the console that joins is this cartridge, checked against the version in its game data. Nothing is sent on a mismatch
help.rse-gift:--console-build: whose addresses a hook, a stub or a ROM call is built with: BPRF, BPGF, BPRE, BPGE, BPRS, BPGS, BPRD, BPGD, BPRI, BPGI, BPRJ, BPGJ. auto (the default) builds for each and sends the one the console's game code names, before anything address-dependent is sent; another code is refused. A game code serves only that cartridge. Bytes with no build address go to any console either way
help.rse-gift:--chain-step: with --buffer-script call-chain: one step, repeatable, up to 16, run in order in one frame. `call:NAME_OR_ADDR[,ARG]...` calls a ROM function (AddBagItem, AddMoney, AddPCItem, CalcCRC16, CheckBagHasItem, CheckBagHasSpace, CompactPartySlots, CreateMon, FlagClear, FlagGet, FlagSet, GetMoney, GetSetPokedexFlag, GetVarPointer, IncrementGameStat, InitRamScript, IsEnoughMoney, ItemIsMail, Random, ReadFlash, RemoveBagItem, RemoveMoney, RunScriptImmediately, SeedRng, SpeciesToNationalPokedexNum, StringCompare, VarGet, VarSet, or a THUMB address); `read32|read16|read8:ADDR` reads; `write32|write16|write8:ADDR,VALUE` writes and reads itself back, and needs --write-unsafe. A target of `prev` is the PREVIOUS step's result and `prev+N` is N bytes past it, which is how a function that returns a pointer becomes a write; an op may carry +keep to leave prev alone. Example: --chain-step call:GetVarPointer,0x4024 --chain-step write16:prev,7. A named function is resolved on the console's build
help.rse-gift:--create-mon-call: with --buffer-script create-mon: the ROM function to call with eight arguments, a THUMB pointer. The default is the console build's CreateMon (0x08041151 French, 0x080411FD English); 0 calls nothing, which checks the send path with the ROM left out
help.rse-gift:--create-mon-species: with --buffer-script create-mon: the species number, 1..411 (internal numbering, not the National Dex)
help.rse-gift:--create-mon-iv: with --buffer-script create-mon: every IV set to this, 0..31. 32 or more rolls them instead [USE_RANDOM_IVS], which makes the run non-deterministic
help.rse-gift:--create-mon-personality: with --buffer-script create-mon: the 32-bit personality value, which fixes the nature, the gender, the ability slot and, with the trainer ids, whether the mon is shiny. Omitted, the console rolls one with Random32
help.rse-gift:--create-mon-ot-id-type: with --buffer-script create-mon: 0 = the OT is the player and the id comes off the real save, 1 = use --create-mon-ot-id, 2 = rolled until not shiny
help.rse-gift:--create-mon-ot-id: with --buffer-script create-mon --create-mon-ot-id-type 1: the OT id to use
help.rse-gift:--create-mon-append: with --buffer-script create-mon: append the finished mon to the player's party. The slot is computed from gSaveBlock1Ptr, never given, and it is always the first free one - playerParty[playerPartyCount] - so an occupied slot is never touched and no Pokemon can be destroyed. A full party writes nothing and says so. This is the player's live SAVE and the console commits it to flash: needs --write-unsafe
help.rse-gift:--create-mon-append-dry-run: with --buffer-script create-mon: the same run as --create-mon-append - the same call, the same arithmetic on the same gSaveBlock1Ptr - with the two stores that would change the save left out. It reports the party count and the address it would have written, and reads that slot's current 100 bytes back so the answer says what a real run would overwrite. Writes nothing, so it needs no override
help.rse-gift:--create-mon-destination: with --buffer-script create-mon: copy the finished 100 bytes to this address in the console's memory. The mon is built in our own image either way, so without this nothing on the console is written at all. Needs --write-unsafe
help.rse-gift:--write-text: with --buffer-script save-write: ascii to write into the save block at --dump-offset. The same region is read back in the same run, so the answer is the proof. The console saves afterwards, so it reaches flash
help.rse-gift:--write-hex: with --buffer-script save-write: the bytes to write, as hex
help.rse-gift:--flash-sector: with --buffer-script flash-write: the 4 KB flash sector (0..31) swi 0x48 writes. Sectors 0..27 are the two save bands and need --write-unsafe; 28..31 are outside both
help.rse-gift:--flash-fill-base: with --buffer-script flash-write: word[0] of the pattern the console composes
help.rse-gift:--flash-fill-step: with --buffer-script flash-write: added to each word of the pattern
help.rse-gift:--flash-words: with --buffer-script flash-write: how many words of the sector to compose
help.rse-gift:--flash-footer: with --buffer-script flash-write: compose a WELL-FORMED save sector instead of a raw pattern - the console zeroes past the data, computes the game's own checksum over the 3968-byte data area and lays down id, checksum, signature and counter
help.rse-gift:--flash-id: with --flash-footer: the sector id written at +0xFF4
help.rse-gift:--flash-counter: with --flash-footer: the save counter written at +0xFFC
help.rse-gift:--flash-derive: with --flash-footer: read gLastWrittenSector and gSaveCounter on the console and write the sector the --flash-id actually occupies right now, rather than a position computed when the payload was built. Needs --write-unsafe
help.rse-gift:--svc-number: with --buffer-script sloop-svc: a syscall, 0x40..0x62 (0x4D is the bad-word check); repeat for up to eight, issued in order in one session
help.rse-gift:--svc-arg: with --buffer-script sloop-svc: r0, r1, r2, r3 in order (repeatable)
help.rse-gift:--svc-text: with --buffer-script sloop-svc: up to 256 bytes of UTF-8 data to send
help.rse-gift:--svc-hex: with --buffer-script sloop-svc: the data as hex instead
help.rse-gift:--resident: with --buffer-script install-resident: the hook to install (turbo)
help.rse-gift:--resident-param: with --buffer-script install-resident: a hook parameter, e.g. extra=6
help.rse-gift:--svc-bkpt: with --buffer-script sloop-svc: issue THUMB `bkpt N` instead of `swi N` (0xFF is the one the game never issues; needs --write-unsafe)
help.rse-gift:--svc-data-in: with --buffer-script sloop-svc: point this register at the console's copy of the data
help.rse-gift:--flash-read-offset: with --buffer-script flash-read: byte offset into the sector to start reading at
help.rse-gift:--flash-patch-offset: with --buffer-script flash-patch: byte offset of the field inside the sector's data
help.rse-gift:--flash-patch-hex: with --buffer-script flash-patch: the replacement bytes for that field, as hex. Everything else in the sector is whatever the game's own save routine wrote
help.rse-gift:--flash-position: with --flash-derive: aim at band position N (0..13) and derive the ID from it, instead of deriving the position from --flash-id. Position 13 is the sector whose counter GetSaveValidStatus reports for the whole slot
help.rse-gift:--flash-counter-bias: with --flash-derive: added to gSaveCounter for the footer. 0 keeps the sector in its own band; a positive value is what would outrank the live slot
help.rse-gift:--write-unsafe: allow a save write outside struct SaveBlock2's never-read filler regions. This is the player's live save and the console commits it to flash; without this the write is refused
help.rse-gift:--flag-id: Wonder Card flagId, 1000..1019; without this option, the selected gift's registered default shown below is used
help.rse-gift:--questionnaire:
require the console to be holding this four-word Easy Chat phrase in its Poke Mart
questionnaire before anything is sent [SVR_CHECK_QUESTIONNAIRE]. Each word is an
English word name, `species:N`, `move:N`, `group/index`, or a raw id. Word ids are
per-language outside the species and move groups, so read the phrase off the target
console first: every session logs the four ids it is holding.
help.rse-gift:--denied-message: what a console that does not know the phrase reads (max 63 characters); the default is 'That is not the phrase.'
help.rse-gift:--hunt-nature:
with --gift rng-mon-hunt: which natures the search will accept, comma separated
(Hardy, Lonely, Brave, Adamant, Naughty, Bold, ...), or plain ids. Without this it takes any.
help.rse-gift:--hunt-iv:
with --gift rng-mon-hunt: a floor under one IV, repeatable (speed=31, attack=20). The stats
are hp, attack, defense, speed, sp_attack, sp_defense, named in the order the ROM draws them - which is not the order the summary
screen shows.
help.rse-gift:--event-pokemon:
with --gift event-pokemon: a fresh copy of a Gen 3 distribution, made by PKHeX by that event's
own PID/IV method, e.g. "WISHMKR Jirachi", "10 ANIV Pikachu", "Aura Mew". The
release in --language is preferred. Without it the card sends a stored WISHMKR Jirachi.
help.rse-gift:--hunt-cap:
with --gift rng-mon-hunt: how many states the stub may try before giving up and leaving the
rng alone. The default is the smallest cap that finds one 99 times in 100.
help.rse-gift:--hunt-species:
with --gift rng-mon-hunt: what the stub's own `setwildbattle` puts on the screen. Neither the
species nor the level is drawn from the rng, so this changes nothing about the
search. The default is a level 5 MAGIKARP, which is catchable in one ball.
help.rse-gift:--hunt-level: with --gift rng-mon-hunt: the level that species appears at.
help.rse-gift:--ram-script-map-group:
which map group the RAM script binds to (a group_order index in
[decomp:data/maps/map_groups.json]). The default is the player's house, where the
mother never moves. Cerulean Cave B1F is group 1 map 74, and MEWTWO is object 3.
help.rse-gift:--ram-script-map-num: which map in that group the RAM script binds to.
help.rse-gift:--ram-script-object:
which object event on that map. Local ids are assigned in map.json order and start
at 1. Binding REPLACES that object's own script, so choose one that never moves.
help.rse-gift:--hunt-freeze-frames:
with --gift rng-mon-hunt: how long the search may block the overworld in the worst case,
in frames (default 900, about 15 s). The field engine has not returned while it
searches, so the player sees a still frame with the music playing; criteria whose
search could take longer than this are refused before the card is built.
help.rse-gift:--news-id: override the news id (1..65535). A console keeps news only when it differs from what it already holds [IsWonderNewsSameAsSaved], so bump this to re-send the same text to the same console
help.rse-gift:--client-ready-idle-frames: diagnostic: quiet child polls after LinkPlayer standby before the first Mystery Gift message; default is the built-in timing
help.rse-gift:--inter-block-gap-frames: diagnostic: idle VBlanks between the blocks of one Mystery Gift message; raise it if a run stalls part-way through a message (default is the built-in timing)
help.rse-gift:--block-repeat: emit each block fragment N times (1-8, default 2); bounded redundancy against the console's silent datagram drops
help.rse-gift:--ram-script-block-repeat: fragment redundancy for the ident-25 delivery script alone (1-8, default 3); the console never reflects gift blocks, so a lost fragment cannot be resent
help.rse-gift:--no-end-on-success: stop after the post-delivery RFU close sequence; used by the supervised run_mystery_gift.sh host
help.rse-gift:--idle-timeout: stop after this many seconds without meaningful Switch traffic (join or Pia/RFU datagram); default: disabled
help.rse-gift:--attempt-log-dir: append completed joined-attempt records to daily csv files in DIR; default: disabled (the supervised shell host enables logs/)
help.rse-gift:--game-data-log: append what the console says about itself - its card counters, its four questionnaire words and its Easy Chat battle profile - to this jsonl ledger. tools/frlg/game_data_read.py reads it back and says what moved between sessions
help.rse-gift:--no-make-artifact: write an annotated listing for the exact Mystery Gift bytes that will be sent (default: disabled)
help.rse-gift:--print-effective-config: print the safe effective host configuration and exit
help.rse-gift:--id: decimal trainer ID, optionally followed by decimal secret ID
help.rse-gift:--card-flag-id: the Wonder Card flag id our trainer card claims in the Union Room card exchange. A console holding the card with that id arms its own card counters, so a trade or cable-club battle with us increments them [union_room.c:1777]; default 0, which arms nothing
help.rse-gift:--no-trust-pia: use Pia-backed send-once block delivery (recommended); --no-trust-pia enables diagnostic RFU retransmits
help.rse-gift:--verbose: show detailed protocol logging instead of milestones
help.rse-gift:--password: LDN passphrase hex; default uses the frlg emulator value
help.rse-gift:--adapter: named Wi-Fi adapter profile used while --phy is auto
help.rse-gift:--over-ip: host for an emulated console over the LAN instead of over the radio: answer ldn_mitm discovery on port 11452 and carry Pia over UDP. Takes the address to advertise, or auto. Needs no adapter, no prod.keys and no root
help.rse-gift:--capture: record an optional JSONL protocol diagnostic
help.rse-gift:--scene: LDN scene; default is the known FRLG scene
help.rse-gift:--no-skip-encryption: delegate transmit CCMP to mac80211/hardware; over-air frames remain encrypted
help.rse-gift:--no-accept-decrypted-ccmp: accept hardware-decrypted RX frames that retain their CCMP header and mic (TP-Link Archer T3U/rtw88_8822bu profile)
help.rse-gift:--no-native-nonce-sequence: use FireRed's session-wide incrementing Pia nonce
help.rse-gift:--no-session-response-first: send Session type 2 unicast before type 5 broadcast
help.rse-gift:--tick-hz: how many RFU slots a second the host emits (default 59.727, one per GBA VBlank). A real console pair runs far below this; lowering it slows every link step by the same factor.
help.lgpe-host:--player-name: the nickname our connection response carries
help.lgpe-host:--channel: 1, 6, 11; code (default): the channel the link code puts a searching console on, the only one it joins on; auto: scan for the console's own network under our scene id and host on its channel
help.lgpe-host:--code: the link code the player enters: three picker names (English or French) or indices 0-9, comma-separated
help.lgpe-host:--no-skip-encryption: let the LDN layer encrypt in software. The Archer T3U wants the hardware path, which is the default here
help.lgpe-host:--no-accept-decrypted-ccmp: do not accept the frames rtw88 has already decrypted. With this the host reads nothing on that adapter
help.lgpe-host:--capture: every datagram, one JSON line each
help.lgpe-host:--variable-id: our own variable id, any nonzero value
help.lgpe-host:--protocol: the LDN advertisement protocol. A title sees only its own: Let's Go advertises and scans on 1, measured off the console's own beacon
help.lgpe-host:--random-ssid: let the LDN layer pick the session id. A Let's Go network's is the fixed value every console advertises, which is the default here
help.lgpe-host:--first: our kind-1 identity message, sent when the console's arrives: a captured 376-byte message, header included, or echo for the console's own back
help.lgpe-host:--trainer-name: the player name our identity carries, the one the trade screen shows
help.lgpe-host:--our-trainer: the trainer id pair written over the identity's
help.lgpe-host:--scene-id: the advertised scene id, in place of the one --code gives
help.lgpe-host:--received: write the peer's offered PB7 here
help.lgpe-host:--fresh-pid: offer every --offer and --next-offer structure under a new PID and encryption constant, shiny state kept, so a save that took it before takes it again
help.lgpe-host:--offer: answer the console's offer with this 232-byte box structure (echo: its own back), and its commits with commits
help.lgpe-host:--next-offer: 232-byte box structure for the next trade in the same session; repeatable, one per trade after the first
help.lgpe-host:--no-type4-data: publish no clone data on clone types 4 and 1. Without it the console never passes the gate at 0x11b080 and stays on its search screen
help.lgpe-host:--drive-delay: seconds between the steps the host drives an offered clone through
help.lgpe-host:--grace: seconds past --seconds to hold a session whose trade is half done
help.lgpe-host:--first-copies: how many kind 1 identities to send, 0.3 s apart under successive steps
help.lgpe-host:--advance-after: seconds after the party clones to move our state word to 2 and send the offer, which is what a station does as its own state word reaches 2
help.lgpe-host:--party-clones: how many party clones (ids 2 up) to announce after the identities; the reference host announced two
help.lgpe-host:--party-clones-delay: seconds after our identity to announce them
help.lgpe-host:--result-after: seconds after the second commit to send the result, the next trade's first slot, with two clones announced 0.5 s before it; a retail host sent it 26.8 s after, behind its trade animation
help.lgpe-host:--ignore-clone0-answer: test only: ignore the console's first answer to our clone 0 pair, as if lost, so the pair goes again
help.lgpe-host:--withhold-announce: test only: skip the first N of our announcements to the console alone, as if lost, so the resend carries them
help.lgpe-host:--lead: test only, for bin/lgpe_join.py: act as a console host's player, each step this many seconds after the last. Offer unprompted after the party clones and after each result, vote on the offered clone, announce and vote the commit clone, commit (docs/lgpe_session.md). Never against a console
help.lgpe-host:--agree-withdrawn-vote: test only: carry the drive on through a withdrawn vote, as the host did before it answered state 2 (docs/lgpe_session.md). Locks a console's save
help.lgpe-host:--ip-host: host over ldn_mitm for an emulator instead of the radio (docs/ldn.md)
help.lgpe-host:--online: trade with a player far away: their console's offer is offered here, and each side confirms only once both consoles have (docs/online.md)
help.lgpe-host:--online-code: the room both players enter; default the link code, and no code meets anyone else trading online without one
help.lgpe-host:--gift-event: the Mystery Gift card each --offer and --next-offer was made from, in the same order: its key in PKHeX's event database (pokeldn.pokemon.Service.gift_events)
help.lgpe-host:--for-receiver: make each --gift-event card that gives the receiver's own trainer again for the console's save, during the trade: the console offers first, a Pokemon its save caught names the trainer, and ours goes up made for it; for any other, the trainer the console's session data names. Failing both, the offer goes as given, under the trainer from Settings (pokeldn.receiver_gift, docs/gift_simulated.md)
help.lgpe-host:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
help.lgpe-join:--print-packets: print every packet in and out; the --capture file keeps them either way
help.lgpe-join:--comm-id: local_communication_id to join, hex. Omit to join the only unknown one
help.lgpe-join:--scan-seconds: keep scanning this long for a console before giving up
help.lgpe-join:--capture: jsonl of every datagram seen while seated, hex, with its verdict
help.lgpe-join:--connect: send a version-9 station connection request to the host and classify the reply, retransmitting every 0.5 s the way Pia does. Without it, listen only
help.lgpe-join:--variable-id: our own variable id, any nonzero value (the console's is random)
help.lgpe-join:--connect-seconds: how long to retransmit the connection request and listen for its reply
help.lgpe-join:--grace: seconds past --connect-seconds or --hold to keep a seat whose trade is half done: a trade left mid-way locks the console out of trading
help.lgpe-join:--player-name: the nickname the connection response carries, what the console shows as the partner (a real station sends its Switch profile's)
help.lgpe-join:--short-response: send the 0x3c-byte connection response instead of the full 0x348-byte one, which carries no network id and no player
help.lgpe-join:--public-address: put our own address in the station location's public field as well as its private one. A Let's Go joiner leaves the public field empty
help.lgpe-join:--nat-location: send nat flags 5 and nat location 1. A Let's Go joiner sends zero for both on local wireless
help.lgpe-join:--reliable-payload: files, comma-separated, holding the game payloads to send on the Reliable Protocol (0x7c) once the clone elements are up; by default the recorded identity in pokeldn.lgpe.reference, and an empty value sends nothing there
help.lgpe-join:--no-rtt: once in the mesh, do not answer the host's RTT requests and send none of our own. Default: answer them and send one a second
help.lgpe-join:--no-sync-clock: once in the mesh, do not run the Sync Clock Protocol (0x1c): a request every 2 s, the host's reply carrying the mesh clock in ms. Default: run it
help.lgpe-join:--no-clone: once in the mesh, do not run the clone clock exchange (requests every 0.2 s, replies with our ms clock, participate after ten answers: docs/lgpe_session.md). Default: run it
help.lgpe-join:--over-ip: reach the peer over plain UDP instead of the radio: no scan, no LDN association, the Pia socket straight at --host-ip:12345. For an emulated host under a debugger. Needs --app-data, --host-mac, --our-mac
help.lgpe-join:--host-mac: the hosting station's MAC, as it appears in its own advertisement
help.lgpe-join:--our-mac: the MAC we present; any value the host has not seen
help.lgpe-join:--app-data: the host's advertise data as hex, or @FILE, instead of scanning for it. Needs --host-mac alongside
help.lgpe-join:--discover-timeout: how long to wait for the scan response and the sync
help.lgpe-join:--ack-peer-clock: carry the peer's announcement clock in our acknowledgement on clone type 2 rather than the clock round-tripped from our own announcement, which is what a reference joiner carries
help.lgpe-join:--trainer-name: the player name our identity carries, the one the trade screen shows
help.lgpe-join:--our-trainer: replace the trainer id pair in the first message. A payload captured between two emulators that share a save carries the host's own pair, which presents the joiner as the station it is trading with
help.lgpe-join:--leave-after: leave the session the way a console backs out of its trade screen, this long after the first trade step we answered (docs/lgpe_session.md)
help.lgpe-join:--stall-leave: leave the way a console backs out when both players have voted and the host has not agreed for this long, before any commit; 0 never. It ends the wait, not the trade lock a confirmed trade already saved
help.lgpe-join:--received: write the peer's offered PB7 here
help.lgpe-join:--fresh-pid: offer every --offer structure under a new PID and encryption constant, shiny state kept, so a save that took it before takes it again
help.lgpe-join:--offer: answer the host's offers with a box structure of our own. 'echo' returns the host's own, which the game accepts by construction; a path is a 232-byte structure, encrypted or not. Repeatable, one per trade on the seat; trade N writes what it received to --received with -N. After the last, a further trade is not answered and the player backs out
help.lgpe-join:--withhold-announce: test only: skip the first N of our announcements to the host alone, as if lost, so the resend carries them
help.lgpe-join:--withhold-clone0-answer: test only: send no answer to the host's first clone 0 pair (0xa1, 0xb1), as if lost, to see whether the host repeats it
help.lgpe-join:--ack-re-announce: answer a peer re-announcement with an acknowledgement carrying its clock rather than a second take-over. A reference joiner takes a clone over once and never again
help.lgpe-join:--publish-delay: seconds after the take-over burst to publish our copy, with --publish-on-announce. Zero puts it in the burst's own frame
help.lgpe-join:--publish-once: answer only the first of a peer's repeated publishes with a copy of our own and acknowledge the rest. Measured to stop the peer publishing at all, so the default answers each one
help.lgpe-join:--own-takeover-clock: stamp our own clock on the take-over instead of the clock the peer's announcement carried. The peer completes a take-over only when it matches the sequence it allocated, so the echo is the default
help.lgpe-join:--announce-after-burst: send the announcement of our own copy a tick after the take-over burst. Both stations of a session that works put all seven in one frame, which is the default here
help.lgpe-join:--publish-on-announce: publish our copy of a clone on clone type 2 as part of the announce burst. A real joiner waits for the peer to publish its own copy first, which is the default here
help.lgpe-join:--publish-fallback: publish anyway this many seconds after the announce if the peer never published its own copy. Not a measured value
help.lgpe-join:--peer-announce-dest: address our own clone announce to the peer alone. A real joiner addresses the first announce of a clone to the whole mesh (dest 0x0003), which is the default here
help.lgpe-join:--clone-requests: answered clock requests of our own before the participate (measured 10)
help.lgpe-join:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
