help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--rpc-port-answers: answer the trade RPC on its OWN Pia port with its own reliable window. The console sends them on 0x7C port 1; an answer on port 0 lands on a window it does not read them on
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--answer-migration: answer the console's MIGRATION_START on 0x18 port 1 with a MIGRATION_RESPONSE. `440001` arrives there only when the player accepts, and the console goes silent on every window afterwards: the last thing it asks for is two bytes of mesh, not application data
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--leave-with-host: when the hosting console leaves, ack its update session carrying the host-migration state and leave the network on its START_HOST_MIGRATION, as its own clients do; each step waits 10 s unanswered
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--migration-answer: what to send when the console migrates the mesh. "auto" sends MIGRATION_FINISH when the start names US as the next host and a MIGRATION_RESPONSE when it names anyone else, which is what the binary says. "response" always answers 0x48, for comparison
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--open-content: after our offer is acknowledged, send `ping` on content N's 10000-base holder for each N - `382700000a00` for 40, which is exactly the opener nxldn-lab's client sends to start the confirmation phase, rebuilt here from our own content registry rather than copied
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--confirm-command: when the CONFIRMATION envelope (40040) sends a four-byte status whose body ends `0100` - the same cue the selection content sends before its Pokemon - reply with SyncSaveDataHolder{syncCommand{data:N}} on that content's 10000-base holder, id 10040, reliable port 0, and answer the status itself on port 1. Content 40 takes a command and not a Pokemon: its parser 0x010df6d0 accepts one submessage carrying one int32. Its own machine sends 0, 1, 2 and 3 in that order (swsh_trade.SYNC_COMMANDS)
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--confirm-phase: answer the confirmation content's four-byte steps with phase N in the LOW u16 instead of echoing the console's own. The console reads its phase out of exactly those bytes (`0x006d6490` stores them, `0x006d3260` reads them), and every step this project has sent so far echoed the value back unchanged
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--abort-on-stall: once the confirmation ladder has produced its first step, end the run as soon as SECONDS pass with no NEW step body: stop transmitting, drop the link and let the console report a lost connection. Holding a stalled ladder open with acks instead makes the game declare the TRADE failed, which costs the player about an hour. Nothing but acks follows the last step body. 0 is off and the hold runs in full.
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--confirm-commands: the handshake form of --confirm-command: send the NEXT of these on each new four-byte body the confirmation content puts on elementId 20000. Content 40's own machine sends 0,1,2,3 and parks after each; one command buys two rungs and then the ladder stops
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--confirm-final-delta: after the CONFIRMATION content answers our syncCommand with a hash, re-arm the 40040 pair and send BOTH members again at this clock delta - the move --selection-final-delta makes on 40050, which carries the selection phase past its own hash
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--selection-final-del: after the selection HASH is answered, send the 40050 pair AGAIN - both members - at this clock delta. nxldn-lab's `selection_final_delta` is 9 (nxldn-lab's `selection_final_delta`). --rpc-pair latches per envelope, so the second pair needs the latch cleared. 0 is off
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--open-content-offer: make --open-content send our PK8 on the 10000-base holder instead of an empty `ping`. The ping opens content 50 and is taken as our Pokemon: the console reaches the confirmation phase and asks the player to trade theirs for an egg. Same moment, same holder, a Pokemon in it
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--box-on-accept: send these box commands the moment MIGRATION_START arrives - the only signal that says the player pressed accept. The console keeps acking for about five seconds after it
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--box-period: seconds between the queued post-offer payloads. Spread them so the sweep spans the accept: the console tears down on the accept, not on a timer, so commands sent inside a couple of seconds all land before it
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--selection-offer: when the console follows its selection-phase Pokemon with the status whose body ends `0100`, offer OUR Pokemon on that content's 10000-base holder (id 10050) on reliable port 0 and answer the status on port 1
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--pair-after-hash: once a hash body has been answered, open content N's phase by sending the two-member RPC pair for it (40 is the confirmation). A pair is the only shape that opens a phase on this console: 40030 opened the offer and 40050 the selection. A bare content ping (`382700000a00`) and a bare sync-120 ping (`780000000a00`) are both ignored
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--sync-after-offer: queue a sync on holder N right behind our selection offer, in the branch that actually runs when --selection-offer is on. --sync-after-hash cannot fire there: this one can
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--sync-field: which SyncPingDataHolder field --sync-after-hash sends: 1 ping, 2 pingReply, 3 pingSynced (`780000001a00`, the one the trace records)
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--sync-after-hash: once a hash body has been answered, send `ping` on sync holder N (120 is the confirmation's) on port 0. The console drives 97, 60000, 110 and 130 itself and opens the selection phase when 130's pingSynced lands; it never sends 120. A phase follows its sync, not a content ping
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--open-after-hash: once a hash body has been answered, `ping` content N's 10000-base holder on port 0 to open the next phase - 40 is the confirmation, so this sends `382700000a00`. The console stops sending 40050 once the hash answer lands and says nothing further; Pia retransmits anything it still waits on, so that silence means satisfied and the next phase needs opening
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--rpc-bodies: answer every DISTINCT (envelope, base, field-5 body) in the 40000 band once, on top of the opening pair. The clock advances on every message so the payload cannot be the key, but the body can: `00000000` and `000018fc` are the openers and anything else is new. A per-envelope guard stops answering at the hash body and stalls there
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--rpc-pair: answer the console's 40030 RPC as the PAIR it is: collect both members one per base, 10000 then 20000, keyed on the BASE FIELD. `payload[5] in (0x19, 0x1A)` is the inner length and moves with the sender's station-id varint (0x1A/0x1B on some consoles). Send both once in that order and nothing more on this window; `said_by_port` keeps only the last payload, so a mirror sends one member repeatedly and never the other
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--open-early: `ping` content N's 10000-base holder at the 0x84 snapshot ack, before either side offers. The console's box send is gated on a ready bool at content+0x4c that only `0x010ce040` sets, on a zero result code; until then every command the game tries to send is parked in content+0x48. A parked command that does not match the next one sets the error byte +0x4d, and `0x010c9bb0` turns that into trade state 9: abort, with nothing on the application layer
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--box-open: send these box commands as soon as the console acks our 0x84 snapshot - BEFORE either side offers a Pokemon. The game sends command 3 exactly once, on the first frame after its trade session is built and only when the role bit at session+0x419 is clear (0x010c9bb0), so one of the two sides owes the other an opener before anything else happens. Sent after both offers instead, the console leaves while the player is still picking
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--box-commands: after our offer is acknowledged, send boxSyncStateCommand{data:N} on the trade holder for each N in turn, one per acknowledged sequence. 20030 is a BoxSyncStateDataHolder and its field 2 is a command enum; this project 1 offers and 2 withdraws; 4 confirms and 5 withdraws the confirmation
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--snapshot-account: replace the three ids at the front of the snapshot's profile (pseudo device id, account Uid, network service account id). They are the console's own, handed back unchanged otherwise
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--selection-offer-dat: with --selection-offer, answer the console's selection status with our PK8 in field 5 (`body`) of a 40050 Data carrying OUR ownerId, on the RPC port, instead of a PokemonTradeDataHolder on 10050 port 0. Content 50's receive handler resolves the sender to a station index and drops silently when it cannot; the holder shape carries no owner
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--selection-offer-swe: send our PK8 as a Data on elementId 10000 and as a holder on the 30000-base id (30050), which every content registers. More than one variable at once
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--selection-offer-hig: with --selection-offer, answer the selection status with our PK8 as a PokemonTradeDataHolder on the 20000-base holder (id 20050), which is where the BOX phase's own Pokemon rides one content over. Overrides --selection-offer-mirror and --selection-offer-data
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--selection-offer-mir: with --selection-offer, answer the selection status with our PK8 in a 40050 carrying the console's OWN field set - syncId, clock, body, and neither elementId nor ownerId, which is how its own selection offer decodes. Overrides --selection-offer-data
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--offer-echo: offer back the exact PK8 the console just offered us, unchanged, instead of one out of --send-snapshot. These bytes came out of its own save, so a run that still aborts rules the record out
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--offer-on-50: put our PK8 in field 5 of the 40050 pair's second member. Content 50 is PokemonTradeDataHolder, the transfer; content 30 is the box exchange. A 344-byte PK8 rides that field
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--send-selection: WHEN to open the selection phase with a 40050 pair on 0x7c port 1. "offer" sends it as soon as our offer is acknowledged, the only window the console is still reading in; "migration" sends it on the migration start, after the console has stopped. The pair is the same envelope as the console's own 40030 at offset 50 with our station id; the builder reproduces its 40030 pair byte for byte
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--update-mesh: once the migration makes us the host, broadcast UPDATE_MESH the way the console did: its own last one with the host index set to ours. The console stops sending these once it hands the role over, and the mesh is gone about 1.3 s later if nothing takes over
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--update-mesh-period: how often to broadcast it; the console sent one about every 2 s
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--migration-period: how often to retransmit the migration response until it is acked
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--answer-once: answer each payload the console sends ONCE instead of re-deriving an answer to its last payload every period. `said` never clears, so without this an offer goes out hundreds of times. The console sends each of its own messages once
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--offer-slot: which party slot of --send-snapshot to offer back, 1-6; 0 offers nothing and only records what the console offers us
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--offer-file: a .pk8 to put in --offer-slot in place of the snapshot's record: stored or party form, encrypted or PKHeX's decrypted export. Its OT name and ids become the snapshot's unless --offer-file-as-is. Repeatable, one per trade on the session: the console's player picks again from the box; the last serves every later trade
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--fresh-pid: draw a new encryption constant and PID for every offered Pokemon
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--offer-file-as-is: keep the file's own OT name and trainer ids
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--offer-species: build the record in --offer-slot instead of sending it as it came: this national dex number, in the party record the snapshot advertises AND in the offer, so the two still tell one story
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--offer-ability: the ability id of the built record; --offer-species leaves the template's ability where it was
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--offer-level: the level byte at 0x148 of the built record, 1..100; the experience word is left alone unless --offer-experience is given
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--offer-experience: the experience word at 0x10 of the built record
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--offer-moves: four move ids, comma-separated; 0 empties a slot. PP is left as the template had it
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--offer-nickname: the nickname of the built record; sets the nicknamed flag
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--offer-ot: the original trainer name of the built record
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--offer-ivs: six IVs, comma-separated, in PKHeX's HP,ATK,DEF,SPE,SPA,SPD order
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--save-offer: write the PK8 we will offer to this file, before the radio is touched
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--save-offered: write the PK8 the console offers to this file; trade N > 1 writes FILE-N
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--rpc-clock-delta: how far to advance a trade RPC's clock in our answer. 5 is nxldn-lab's and is the one number in this path nothing here has measured
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--rpc-pair-advance: after answering an RPC pair, send BOTH members again with the clock advanced by this much. The console advances its own pair's clock by 2 each burst (b41c, b61c, b81c). A repeated clock is a repeated state, so an answer that carries one clock never moves ours. 0 is off
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--selection-start: send our own 40050 pair the moment the console says id 130 pingSynced, before its own selection burst. nxldn-lab's client opens the selection phase this way and nothing here has ever opened one; the console sends 820000001a00 in our own captures 0.3 s before its 40050 burst
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--ack-snapshot: ACK the console's 0x84 fragments (kind 0x21, a contiguous base and a bitmask). Nothing here has ever acked this protocol, which is why the console retransmits one snapshot 19142 times and never moves on
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--send-snapshot: a 3456-byte trade snapshot to send back on 0x84 once the console sends its own, or live (the default under --preset trade) for the console's own from this session. A short 2965-byte payload is inflated first. The identity is rewritten by --snapshot-name/-tid/-sid
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--snapshot-port: Pia port(s) for our 0x84 messages; the console sends on 0
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--snapshot-repeat: between whole re-sends; the console retransmits its own until acked
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--sync-answers: answer with `pokeldn.swsh.trade.SYNC_ANSWERS` instead of echoing one payload: the ping, and the three other sync holders the console is expected to raise after the trade snapshot. A payload with no rule is REPORTED and left unanswered - that report is the point of the run
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--send-mirror: send back whatever the console last said on this protocol, rather than the fixed --send-data. --send-data is still the first payload, before the console has said anything
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--send-count: how many sequence ids of ours to send in all; 0 has no limit. One message does not hold the console's state; it sends its own heartbeat about 580 times in 180 s
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--send-period: the retransmit interval. A window retransmits until it is acked
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--send-seconds: how long to keep retransmitting if nothing acknowledges it; 0 sends until the run ends
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--raid-join: a Max Raid den guest: after the snapshot send PlayerInfo, BattleReady and SelectPokemon (the --offer-slot Pokemon); use with --scene 60006
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--lair-join: a Dynamax Adventure (Max Lair) guest: the lobby, the paths and the battles; use with --scene 50000
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--lair-rental: an encrypted party PK8 sent as our rental instead of the offered one
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--lair-rental-choice: the offer place we take; by default the first the host left
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--raid-ready: press ready this many seconds after the host acked the lobby messages
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--raid-move: the move slot our Pokemon uses every turn
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--raid-name: the name the raid lobby shows for us
help.swsh-lan-lair-join:--grace: seconds past --hold to keep a session whose trade is under way: the console has offered and the ladder has not finished
help.bdsp-host:--capture: every datagram and event, one JSON line each
help.bdsp-host:--ldn-protocol: the LDN protocol the advertisement is encrypted for
help.bdsp-host:--scene-id: default the Union Room's, or the password room's with --password
help.bdsp-host:--password: host the room the player enters with this password, e.g. 00000000
help.bdsp-host:--name: the player name our side carries
help.bdsp-host:--variable-id: our Pia variable id; random by default
help.bdsp-host:--at: where our character stands: x,y,z,rot_y (a retail host's own spot)
help.bdsp-host:--state: the OnlineState we report when asked; 4 raises the trade bubble
help.bdsp-host:--fresh-pid: offer it under a new PID and encryption constant, shiny state kept, so a save that took it before takes it again
help.bdsp-host:--offer: the Pokemon we trade: a complete, legal, encrypted 328-byte PB8 whose PID the console's save does not already hold; repeatable, one per trade in order, the last offered again after the list
help.bdsp-host:--complete-trade: answer the ready-ok, after which the console writes its save
help.bdsp-host:--save-theirs: write the Pokemon the console offers in trade N to PREFIX_N.pb8
help.bdsp-host:--approach-delay: seconds after the player's trade emote before our character approaches (no walk)
help.bdsp-host:--online: trade with a player far away: their console's offer is offered here, and each side confirms only once both consoles have (docs/online.md)
help.bdsp-host:--online-code: the room both players enter; default the link code, and no code meets anyone else trading online without one
help.bdsp-host:--gift-event: the Mystery Gift card each --offer was made from, in the same order: its key in PKHeX's event database (pokeldn.pokemon.Service.gift_events)
help.bdsp-host:--for-receiver: make each --gift-event card that gives the receiver's own trainer again for the console's save, during the trade: the console offers first, a Pokemon its save caught names the trainer, and ours goes up made for it; for any other, the trainer the console's session data names. Failing both, the offer goes as given, under the trainer from Settings (pokeldn.receiver_gift, docs/gift_simulated.md)
help.bdsp-host:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
help.bdsp-join:--print-packets: print every packet in and out; the --capture file keeps them either way
help.bdsp-join:--scans: scans for the console's room before giving up; it may not exist yet
help.bdsp-join:--dwell: seconds per channel in the scan; 0.8 missed a live network twice
help.bdsp-join:--language: the PlayerInfo language byte, a MsgLangId (3 is French); 1, 8, 9 and 10 cap the greeting's name at 6 characters, others at 12 (docs/bdsp_protocol.md)
help.bdsp-join:--count: the console's protocol count, if already measured; skips the sweep
help.bdsp-join:--identify: after the count, read each candidate protocol's registered version
help.bdsp-join:--connect: send N well-formed connection requests and report what comes back
help.bdsp-join:--join: after the station handshake, send up to N mesh join requests
help.bdsp-join:--no-reliable-ack: after the join, sweep the bulk acknowledgement until the console's reliable retransmission stops
help.bdsp-join:--room-walk: after the reliable handshake, send N position messages of our own and watch the console's screen
help.bdsp-join:--join-wait: --room-pattern fixed: seconds a join has to draw the console's request for NetCharacterStateData before the next goes out
help.bdsp-join:--room-walk-steps: position messages in the burst pattern's walk. At the console's own stride, 60 is 55.8 units and leaves the Union Room entirely; pass 8 for a walk that ends where the screen can still see it
help.bdsp-join:--room-walk-period: seconds between position messages in the burst pattern. The default is the console's own median gap
help.bdsp-join:--room-walk-stride: units one position message spans. The default is what a console's own walk measures (0.93 units every 0.41 s, over 80 of its messages); our first walks did 0.15 every 0.6 s, which is a ninth of a real player's speed and is the whole of the stutter
help.bdsp-join:--no-answer-requests: answer the console's NetRequestData with the message it names. It has asked for data id 0x23 in every capture since the first join and has never been answered; this is the probe, so arm it on its own
help.bdsp-join:--no-match-wait: answer the console's request for NetDataIsMatchWaitData (0x23) with isMatchWait=1 instead of 0. ONE comparison in UnionRoomManager$$SetNetData gates the trade on it (`cmp w23, #1` at main.bin 0x01fd56e4, then UnionFrontDeskTradeController$$StartMatch); every run has answered 0, which is a station declining to be matched
help.bdsp-join:--no-trade-reply: answer the console's trade messages with ours. It sends a trainer record and then a Pokemon and waits; with neither answered the player sits on "En attente d'une reponse". THIS DOES NOT COMPLETE A TRADE - the player still confirms on their own screen, and declining there leaves the save untouched
help.bdsp-join:--no-complete-trade: answer NetDataTradeReadyOkData (0x21) with tradeState=WAIT and LET THE TRADE COMPLETE. THIS WRITES THE CONSOLE'S SAVE: the message is the only writer of the console's `targetTradeState`, both states at WAIT move UnionTradeManager to SECURIY_TRADE, and TradeStateModel$$InitState calls PlayerSave. The Pokemon the player picked leaves their box and ours takes its place. Needs --trade-reply. ASK THE USER FIRST
help.bdsp-join:--security-repeat: seconds between repeats of our security-phase state, until the console reports SEND_READYOK. A CHILD console's SEND_READYOK only ends when a message arrives inside it
help.bdsp-join:--fresh-pid: offer it under a new PID and encryption constant, shiny state kept, so a save that took it before takes it again
help.bdsp-join:--trade-template: a PB8 to offer (328 or 344 bytes, encrypted or PKHeX's decrypted export), edited by --trade-nickname and --trade-ot. 328 bytes hold much more than this project has identified, so what we send is a real Pokemon with named fields changed rather than one invented from nothing. Repeatable, one per trade in order; the last is offered again after the list
help.bdsp-join:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
help.bdsp-join:--answer-return-select: answer the console's NetDataReturnSelectData, a round reset, ONCE; the answer has no measured effect
help.bdsp-join:--return-select-value: the byte to answer it with (default 0, what a console answers a {1} with [0x1c27f48]; a {1} reads as our back-out and, past phase 2, shows 'the partner canceled the trade')
help.bdsp-join:--trade-ot: OT name for the offered Pokemon
help.bdsp-join:--trade-name: the name in OUR trainer record
help.bdsp-join:--trade-save-poke: where to write the Pokemon the console offers; trade N > 1 writes FILE-N
help.bdsp-join:--join-offset-x: where our character spawns relative to the console's own, on x. The default +2.0 is one fixed side, and a player standing against the wall on that side gets a character spawned out of bounds (followed by a crash). Negative puts it on the other side
help.bdsp-join:--no-initiate-talk: APPROACH the console's character instead of waiting to be approached. Picking an emote locks a player in place waiting to be interacted with, so a recruiting console can only be reached by someone walking up to it. Waits for its broadcast state to say it is advertising, then sends NetDataTalkReserveData - the console's own bytes, 63 00 01 00
help.bdsp-join:--after-approach: after THEY answer our approach, send this message - the initiator's own next one. `0x06:0000000000` is NetDataTalkData{sexId 0, CHECK}, which is what SwitchTalkStateMine builds. Repeatable, sent in order
help.bdsp-join:--after-approach-gap: seconds between the approach answer and each --after-approach message
help.bdsp-join:--initiate-delay: seconds to wait after the console starts advertising before approaching
help.bdsp-join:--initiate-tries: how many times to retransmit the approach before giving up
help.bdsp-join:--match-wait-period: with --match-wait, ALSO send NetDataIsMatchWaitData{1} every S seconds for the whole hold (0 disables, leaving the answer-on-request). The console requests 0x23 once, at t=8.4-9.4, and the player reaches the trade option in the Y menu long after that
help.bdsp-join:--after-talk: after answering the talk reservation, send this game message on the reliable stream - `0x08:00` is NetDataSelectData{index: 0}. Repeatable, sent in order. The console parks in TalkState GREETING and waits to be advanced, and which message does it is not readable offline: this is the sweep handle
help.bdsp-join:--after-talk-gap: seconds between the talk answer and each --after-talk message
help.bdsp-join:--no-answer-talk: answer a NetDataTalkReserveData with a NetDataTalkReserveResultData. unanswered, the player's character freezes
help.bdsp-join:--can-talk: NetDataTalkReserveResultData.IsCanTalk - 1 accepts the talk, 0 refuses it. A refusal is the SAFE probe: it should release the player rather than open a flow we cannot hold up
help.bdsp-join:--state: the OpcState.OnlineState our character reports when the console asks for NetCharacterStateData. 0 NONE means "doing nothing" and is a character doing nothing; 3 RECRUITMENT_BATTLE, 4 RECRUITMENT_TRADE, 5 RECRUITMENT_RECORD, 6 RECRUITMENT_GREETINGS, 8 COMMUNICATE
help.bdsp-join:--recruiting: StateData.isRecruiment, the second byte of the same answer
help.bdsp-join:--join-avatar: NetJoinData.avatarId, which is what picks the MODEL: it indexes UnionCharacterTable and OpLoadCharacter loads that asset name. 8 is what the default, the girl the screen shows
help.bdsp-join:--join-color: NetJoinData.colorId. The game also derives one from the avatar id (OpcManager.GetNpcColorId), so this may not be the deciding field
help.bdsp-join:--request-ids: after the walk, send a NetRequestData for each of these data ids, one at a time on the reliable stream, and print what comes back. The Union Room answers six ids (docs/bdsp_protocol.md); 0x22 is the opaque one
help.bdsp-join:--pre-request: a game message to put on the reliable stream before the first --request-ids request, e.g. 0x59:01000100 to add station 1 to the console's match-wait list. Repeatable, sent in order
help.bdsp-join:--no-ug-join: Grand Underground: once the console's NetZoneData arrives, send a NetUgJoinData in its zone at its position plus --join-offset-x/z
help.bdsp-join:--ug-join-delay: seconds after the console's NetZoneData before the Underground join
help.bdsp-join:--answer-with: when the console sends game message ID, answer once with the body in FILE (raw bytes, no header): 0x15:capsule.bin answers its ball capsule with ours, 0x14:record.bin its record
help.bdsp-join:--inject-file: poll this file and send each new `ID:HEX` line as a game message on the reliable window, retransmitted until acked. Lines are sent once, in order; `#` starts a comment
help.bdsp-join:--request-gap: seconds between one request landing and the next going out
help.bdsp-join:--request-delay: seconds after the walk before the first request
help.bdsp-join:--no-send-card: after the walk, send a NetDataTranerCardData for our own station. It is the message that says what a player LOOKS like, and the probe is whether the character the game drew for us changes on screen
help.bdsp-join:--room-pattern: square spawns one avatar per corner; line and fixed ask whether the game's idea of identity is the station or the position
help.bdsp-join:--no-reliable-auto-ack: acknowledge the console's reliable data as it arrives
help.bdsp-join:--reliable-sweep: how many values of the byte at offset 1 to try
help.bdsp-join:--reliable-ack-wait: how long silence has to last to count as an ack that landed
help.bdsp-join:--connect-timeout: how long one connection request waits for its answer
help.bdsp-join:--no-rtt: answer the console's RTT requests (protocol 0x58) while we hold the seat
help.bdsp-join:--no-leave-on-host-migration: leave the network when the console host starts host migration (Local Protocol 0x13), which its player leaving the room sends; a station that stays sees it repeated for 10 s before the console closes its network
help.bdsp-join:--no-join-ack: ack the mesh join response, on the STATION protocol
help.bdsp-join:--join-ack-seconds: how long to keep acking the mesh join response; the host repeats it every 500 ms until it is acknowledged
help.bdsp-join:--ack-repeats: how many times to ack the acceptance; the console repeats it until acked
help.bdsp-join:--sweep-ids: probe all 256 protocol ids, not only the ones the wiki names
help.bdsp-join:--ids: a comma-separated list of ids to probe instead
help.bdsp-join:--vary-var: after identifying, vary the variable id to find what result 7 tests
help.bdsp-join:--gap: seconds to wait for a reply; every probe gets one, so this is short
help.bdsp-join:--probe-id: a protocol id the console does not register, so its version is 0
help.bdsp-join:--probe-version: 1 against an expected 0 is a guaranteed 'version is too high'
help.bdsp-join:--unicast: only the unicast pass, skipping the broadcast one
help.bdsp-join:--broadcast-only: only the broadcast pass, the framing the ack proved

help.pla-host:--capture: write every datagram here as JSON lines
help.pla-host:--app-version: the LDN application version; the console's own is unread
help.pla-host:--ssid: hex, 16 bytes; default lets the LDN layer pick
help.pla-host:--ip-host: host over ldn_mitm on the LAN for an emulator; no radio and no root
help.pla-host:--net-protocol: the Net protocol id to send the connection request under
help.pla-host:--player-name: the LDN node name; a retail console publishes its profile name here
help.pla-host:--rtt-probe: also send an RTT request, which a peer answers with no state at all
help.pla-host:--no-net-probe: stay silent after a join, to measure what the joiner does unprompted
help.pla-host:--our-ip: with --ip-host, the address to advertise and serve on
help.pla-host:--no-session-ack: do not answer a join request with the type-1 ack (buys 8 s, completes nothing)
help.pla-host:--no-session-response: do not answer a join request with the type-2 join response
help.pla-host:--join-seq: the sequence id the join response promises; a type-5 update must reach it
help.pla-host:--session-update: after the response, send a type-5 station-list update (sets job+0x7c). Its per-station layout is provisional pending the 0x739050 decode
help.pla-host:--sustain: once joined, echo RTT and acknowledge the reliable stream so the console does not time out after 12 s and leave
help.pla-host:--reliable-hello: hex: once the console speaks on reliable, send this as the host's own reliable seq-1 data (the game leaves at +10 s if the host never speaks)
help.pla-host:--reliable-mirror: progress the host's reliable stream in lockstep: for each console reliable data message, send the host's own next-sequence data with the same payload (the console advances only as the host advances)
help.pla-host:--hello-protocol: the protocol the host sends its reliable game data on; the game's own reader polls 0x80 (BroadcastReliable), so 0x80 puts data where the game drains it
help.pla-host:--host-player-name: the host's player name in the station-list update, which the game reads as identity; a real name in place of the placeholder single space
help.pla-host:--host-player-id: hex, 16 bytes: the host's player id in the station-list update, a real principal id in place of the placeholder
help.pla-host:--clock: answer the console's clone-clock (0x77) with a host clock message; the console's ClockProtocol is parked in state 4 and an inbound clock message resets its state machine (report 157)
help.pla-host:--atomic-announce: once the mesh is running, send one Atomic (0x74) kind-0 announce; a probe for whether a host announce fills an element slot (report 163)
help.pla-host:--data-exchange: send the host's own record on the 0x81 data exchange once the console opens its stream; the exchange the trade scene is the success branch of
help.pla-host:--data-exchange-name: the player name in that record; the game shows it as the trade partner (default --player-name)
help.pla-host:--data-exchange-id: hex: the four-byte player id in that record
help.pla-host:--gender: 0 male, 1 female: the gender in that record, whose look follows it
help.pla-host:--game-channel: open the game's own reliable channel (0x7c) once the data exchange is done: answer the console's channel message, send the same back, and open the host's own port-0 channel, which is what the trade flow's step 0x20 ticks its network object for
help.pla-host:--trade-box: offer the host's own Pokemon on the game channel: answer the console's trade box with one of ours at sequence 2 on port 0
help.pla-host:--trade-box-ours: offer a record of the host's own rather than the captured one: the same Pokemon under the data exchange's player name and id and a new identity, so the console is not offered the record it is itself holding
help.pla-host:--trade-box-level: the level byte in the offered record's party tail
help.pla-host:--trade-box-experience: the experience in the offered record; the level the game shows is the curve's, so this and --trade-box-level go together
help.pla-host:--trade-box-pid: hex: the personality value in the offered record. HYPOTHESIS: a record is shiny when the trainer id, the secret id and the two halves of this value exclusive-or to under 16, which is the Gen-6 rule and is untested here
help.pla-host:--trade-box-nickname: the nickname in the offered record
help.pla-host:--trade-box-collect: write every record the console shows or offers to this directory, one file per distinct record, named by species and nickname
help.pla-host:--offer-out: write the record the console traded to this file, -N before the extension for trade N above 1
help.pla-host:--fresh-pid: offer the record under a new PID and encryption constant, drawn once per run, shiny state kept, so a save that took it before takes it again
help.pla-host:--trade-box-record: offer this record file instead of the reference one; stored or party, encrypted or decrypted. Repeatable, one per trade in order; the last is offered again after the list
help.pla-host:--interrupt-before-phase-6: after answering phase 3, wait for the console's phase 6, then leave without answering it; this deliberately triggers the game's trade restriction
help.pla-host:--leave-after: seconds after a station's session join to send it the type-3 leave and end the run; the one direction no capture shows
help.pla-host:--leave-sends: how many times to send it; a console sends four
help.pla-host:--stay-after-leave: keep the network up and go silent after the leave instead of ending the run; separates what a console reads in the leave from what it reads in the network going down. Also keeps the run (and BOOT marks) after a console leaves following a trade
help.pla-host:--data-exchange-skip-source-che: put the skip-source-check flag on the record, where a reference host sends none; one variable if a run shows the record is not dispatched
help.pla-host:--data-exchange-record: send this 139-byte record file instead of building one
help.pla-host:--reliable-dest-bits: destination-bit count on the host's reliable message; 2 so the console's own station index (1) is in range of the body destination-bitmap check
help.pla-host:--reliable-bitmap: destination bitmap word, big-endian at wire[9]; the console drops a message unless the bit for its own station index (1) is set, so bit 1 = 0x2
help.pla-join:--ip-join: join over ldn_mitm on the LAN; no radio and no root
help.pla-join:--race: --ip-join: hold one scan socket and connect the instant a fresh network appears, to land before the host latches its node list
help.pla-join:--dwell: seconds per channel in a scan
help.pla-join:--mac: give the board this station MAC first
help.pla-join:--code: the eight digits; '' joins any code
help.pla-join:--name: the LDN node name we publish
help.pla-join:--hold: how long one seat is held
help.pla-join:--player-name: the name in our data exchange record; the console shows it
help.pla-join:--player-id: hex, four bytes: the player id in our data exchange record
help.pla-join:--gender: 0 male, 1 female: the gender in our data exchange record; its look follows
help.pla-join:--join-player-id: hex, sixteen bytes: the player id in the session join request

help.pla-online:--no-net-probe: stay silent after a join, to measure what the joiner does unprompted

help.pla-online:--no-session-response: do not answer a join request with the type-2 join response

help.pla-online:--session-update: after the response, send a type-5 station-list update (sets job+0x7c). Its per-station layout is provisional pending the 0x739050 decode
help.pla-online:--sustain: once joined, echo RTT and acknowledge the reliable stream so the console does not time out after 12 s and leave
help.pla-online:--reliable-hello: hex: once the console speaks on reliable, send this as the host's own reliable seq-1 data (the game leaves at +10 s if the host never speaks)
help.pla-online:--reliable-mirror: progress the host's reliable stream in lockstep: for each console reliable data message, send the host's own next-sequence data with the same payload (the console advances only as the host advances)
help.pla-online:--hello-protocol: the protocol the host sends its reliable game data on; the game's own reader polls 0x80 (BroadcastReliable), so 0x80 puts data where the game drains it
help.pla-online:--host-player-name: the host's player name in the station-list update, which the game reads as identity; a real name in place of the placeholder single space
help.pla-online:--host-player-id: hex, 16 bytes: the host's player id in the station-list update, a real principal id in place of the placeholder
help.pla-online:--clock: answer the console's clone-clock (0x77) with a host clock message; the console's ClockProtocol is parked in state 4 and an inbound clock message resets its state machine (report 157)
help.pla-online:--atomic-announce: once the mesh is running, send one Atomic (0x74) kind-0 announce; a probe for whether a host announce fills an element slot (report 163)
help.pla-online:--data-exchange: send the host's own record on the 0x81 data exchange once the console opens its stream; the exchange the trade scene is the success branch of

help.pla-online:--gender: 0 male, 1 female: the gender in that record, whose look follows it

help.pla-online:--trade-box: offer the host's own Pokemon on the game channel: answer the console's trade box with one of ours at sequence 2 on port 0

help.pla-online:--trade-box-level: the level byte in the offered record's party tail

help.pla-online:--interrupt-before-phase-6: after answering phase 3, wait for the console's phase 6, then leave without answering it; this deliberately triggers the game's trade restriction
help.pla-online:--leave-after: seconds after a station's session join to send it the type-3 leave and end the run; the one direction no capture shows

help.sv-host:--online: trade with a player far away: their console's offer is offered here, and each side confirms only once both consoles have (docs/online.md)

help.sv-host:--capture: write every datagram here as JSON lines
help.sv-host:--violet: advertise Violet's local communication id instead of Scarlet's
help.sv-host:--scene-id: the LDN scene: 4 for a Link Trade, 7 for a Tera Raid
help.sv-host:--max-participants: the LDN participant limit; a Tera Raid advertises 4
help.sv-host:--platform: the station platform byte: 1 is a Switch 2, which is what both retail consoles advertise; 0 is a Switch and what the LDN layer defaults to
help.sv-host:--ssid: hex, 16 bytes; default lets the LDN layer pick
help.sv-host:--ip-host: host over ldn_mitm on the LAN for an emulator; no radio and no root
help.sv-host:--no-leave-response: leave a console's Session type-3 leave request unanswered; it then resends it every 0.5 s and leaves after the fourth (docs/sv.md, Leaving)
help.sv-host:--print-packets: print every packet in and out; the --capture file keeps them either way
help.sv-host:--ack-period: seconds between the periodic bulk acks on every port the console used
help.sv-host:--clock: answer clone clock requests, if any
help.sv-host:--update-seq: the sequence id in the station-list update; a Scarlet host sends 1 where its join response sent 0
help.sv-host:--update-first-seq: also send a station list in the same breath as the join response, under this sequence id; an emulated Scarlet host sends one with id 0 there and the second about two seconds later
help.sv-host:--update-delay: seconds between the Session join response and the station-list update; a Scarlet host leaves about 1.5 s
help.sv-host:--session-flags: the message flags on the Session replies; a Scarlet host sends 0x00, this host's own default is 0x01
help.sv-host:--session-packet-id: the packet id in the Pia header of the Session replies; a Scarlet host's join response carries 1
help.sv-host:--scarlet-response: the 41-byte Session join response a Scarlet host sends, with no route bytes, rather than Arceus's 43-byte one
help.sv-host:--net-flags: the message flags on the Net 0x11 opening; a retail host sends 0x31, this host's own default is 0x01
help.sv-host:--rtt-probe: send an RTT request this often, as a pair's host does every 410 ms; the host otherwise only answers them
help.sv-host:--net-property-flags: the message flags on the Net 0x50; a pair's host sends 0x31 on it and on its 0x11, and this host's 0x11 needs 0x01 to be answered at all
help.sv-host:--net-property: send the Net 0x50 update-property message a pair's host sends 0.37 s after its 0x11, retransmitting until the console's 0x51
help.sv-host:--net-stations: how many 21-byte station slots the Net 0x11 carries; a retail host writes four whatever the game's participant limit is
help.sv-host:--code: the Link Code the player sets, e.g. 12345678; empty for none
help.sv-host:--game-data: hex, the 40 game bytes of the advertisement; a searching console leaves them zero, a host that a joiner reached carried 648cf4 at +0x21
help.sv-host:--send-at: DELAY:PROTO:PORT:HEX[:z][:start|:end], a reliable data message sent that many seconds after the seat; the sequence follows the port's own. A pair's host sends its 0x7c port 1 table update at nine seconds this way
help.sv-host:--record-set: a directory of NNN.bin records to send on 0x81 port 0 as this host's own identity, the way a pair's host sends its 46; the first carries INITIALIZED and every one is already zlib (scratchpad/sv_extract_records.py writes such a set); by default the recorded set in pokeldn.sv.reference
help.sv-host:--trainer-name: the player name record 1 of our identity carries, the one the trade screen shows
help.sv-host:--no-identity: send no station identity unless --record-set or --send-on-open names one; by default the recorded one in pokeldn.sv.reference
help.sv-host:--record-delay: seconds after the seat before the record set goes out
help.sv-host:--records-per-packet: bundle the record set N to a packet, each after the first with its header inherited, as a retail host's retransmit round does (docs/sv.md)
help.sv-host:--record-spacing: seconds between the record packets; a retail raid host spreads its identity over about 0.13 s
help.sv-host:--announce: run the game's port-2 opening from the station ids instead of a replay: the type-7 announcement on 0x80 port 2 carrying this host's own station id, and a type 9 carrying the console's in answer to its type-3 join on 0x7c port 2 (pokeldn.sv.port2)
help.sv-host:--announce-delay: seconds after the seat before the type 7 goes out; a pair's host sends it at about 2.3
help.sv-host:--fresh-pid: offer each record under a new PID and encryption constant, shiny state kept, so a save that took it before takes it again
help.sv-host:--trade-offer: a file holding the 348-byte record this host offers (raw, or hex text; a 352-byte game message is stripped of its header). With it the host answers the console's offer with its own, confirms, and follows the console through the commit and the four exchange steps the way a pair's host does (pokeldn.sv.trade). Repeatable: the second and later records are offered in the same seat, one per trade, as each trade closes
help.sv-host:--gift-event: the Mystery Gift card each --trade-offer was made from, in the same order: its key in PKHeX's event database (pokeldn.pokemon.Service.gift_events)
help.sv-host:--for-receiver: make each --gift-event card that gives the receiver's own trainer again for the console's save, during the trade: the console offers first, a Pokemon its save caught names the trainer, and ours goes up made for it; for any other, the trainer the console's session data names. Failing both, the offer goes as given, under the trainer from Settings (pokeldn.receiver_gift, docs/gift_simulated.md)
help.sv-host:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
help.sv-host:--offer-set: a field written into the offered record before it is sealed, by its pokeldn.sv.pokemon name: nickname=SHINY, species=906, level=50, ivs=31,31,31,31,31,31, pid=0x1234, trainer_id=12345, ball=4, moves=33,0,0,0. Repeatable, and `shiny` alone rolls a personality value shiny against the record's own ids
help.sv-host:--offer-dump: write the offered record's 348-byte body to this file as hex and exit, which needs no radio
help.sv-host:--offer-out: a file to write the console's own offer to, the 348-byte body of its 80 00 02 00 message, as hex text. What it holds is read by pokeldn.sv.pokemon
help.sv-host:--send-on-open: DELAY:PROTO:PORT:HEX[:z][:start|:end], sent that many seconds after the console announces its own key 0x80 open on 0x7c port 1. A port-0 message sent before that open is acknowledged by the console and never reaches the game, and so is everything after it on that port; repeatable; by default the identity fragments in pokeldn.sv.reference
help.sv-host:--offer-after-open: seconds after the console's key-0x80 open at which the host offers first; the same gate as --send-on-open
help.sv-host:--offer-at: seconds after the seat at which the host offers first, before the console does, as a pair's host did; without it the host answers the console's offer
help.sv-host:--confirm-delay: seconds after the console's offer before the host's confirmation
help.sv-host:--raid-seed: host a Tera Raid: the raid seed, eight hex digits; the boss, its Tera type and the rewards follow from it and the four --raid-* context flags
help.sv-host:--raid-pokemon: the party record our player brings to the raid, legal per PKHeX; with --raid-seed
help.sv-host:--raid-reward: a reward row in place of the seed's, in order; up to 45
help.sv-host:--raid-progress: the story stage, which sets a standard crystal's star odds
help.sv-host:--raid-content: a standard or a black (six-star) crystal
help.sv-host:--raid-event: host an event raid: a Poke Portal News delivery's folder (an EventsGallery event, or its Files); the seed draws from the event's encounters at --raid-version and --raid-progress, and --raid-map and --raid-content are unused
help.sv-host:--raid-event-group: the delivery group of the event's den, 1 to 10; by default the first with dens and an encounter at that progress
help.sv-host:--raid-catch-normal: with --raid-event: serve a catch-once encounter (every seven-star raid, Walking Wake, Iron Leaves...) as a normal catch, its capture rate normal and its record number a stand-in no save has caught, so a save that caught it may catch it again; one that cannot be caught stays so (docs/sv_raid.md, Event raids)
help.sv-host:--raid-players: consoles the raid waits for, 1 to 3; it starts once N are in the lobby and every one is Ready, or when the lobby timer runs out
help.sv-host:--raid-partner: an NPC partner the raid seats, in slot order, one per slot the consoles leave empty (2 with one console, 1 with two, none with three): Austin, Ava, Logan, Hailey, Evan, Charlotte, Kylie, Hunter, Gianna, Eli, Henry, Chase, Claire, Brooklyn, Zoe, Samantha, Dylan, Luke; the host draws a partner seed that seats them, the rest drawn freely (docs/sv_raid.md, Partners)
help.sv-host:--raid-partner-progress: the unlock stage the partners come from, which sets their pool, their level being four fifths of --raid-pokemon's; by default --raid-progress's, six stars for a black crystal or a seven-star event raid
help.sv-host:--raid-serve: serve the raid battle from this station with a plugin's battle server (NAME, or the first one loaded): the console and our Pokemon fight one battle; one console only; a failure hands the network over as without it (docs/sv_raid.md, Serving the battle)
help.sv-host:--send: PROTO:PORT:HEX, a reliable data message to send once the console has joined (host seq 1 on that port, INITIALIZED); repeatable
help.sv-join:--print-packets: print every packet in and out; the --capture file keeps them either way
help.sv-join:--code: join only a console searching with this Link Code; empty takes any
help.sv-join:--comm-id: local communication id to join, hex; default is either cartridge's
help.sv-join:--ip-join: join an emulated console over the LAN through ldn_mitm instead of the radio: no root, no phy, no prod.keys
help.sv-join:--scan-timeout: --ip-join: seconds to wait for one ldn_mitm scan answer
help.sv-join:--dwell: seconds per channel in the scan; the console's hosting window is a few seconds, so a long dwell misses it
help.sv-join:--hold: how long to stay in one joined session before scanning again
help.sv-join:--name: the LDN node name we publish
help.sv-join:--platform: the station platform byte we publish; 1 is what a Switch 2 sends
help.sv-join:--mac: set the adapter's MAC before associating, e.g. 48:f1:eb:11:22:33. Pia derives a station's constant id from its MAC, and the two consoles' are Nintendo OUIs where the adapter's is not. The driver reload in the launcher puts the adapter's own address back
help.sv-join:--scene-id: join only a network of this LDN scene: 4 a Link Trade, 7 a Tera Raid
help.sv-join:--raid-pokemon: join the Tera Raid lobby a console hosts and bring this party record, legal per PKHeX; our player readies, answers the start and leaves when the battle begins, its Pokemon fighting on for the console
help.sv-join:--raid-ready-delay: seconds in the raid lobby before our player readies
help.sv-join:--union-circle: join the Union Circle a console hosts, as a raid guest joins a raid: take the seat, send our identity, open the game's channel, answer the host's start, put our player on the field where the host's stands and hold it for --hold (docs/sv_union_circle.md)
help.sv-join:--circle-task: with --union-circle, a task after which our player leaves the circle and the run ends: snacksworth gives the host every Team and solo clear it lacks for all of Snacksworth's legendaries, one a second from the start demo's end; bp a clear paying the host the --bbq-clear BP
help.sv-join:--follow-host: with --union-circle: our player copies the host's as it moves, its animations and its ride, keeping 5 m from it and facing it
help.sv-join:--spawn: with --union-circle: 10 s after the circle's start demo has ended, keep 3 wild Pokemon of this species (dev number) out 15 to 25 m from the host's player, as a console shares its own: one the host battles, removes or goes more than 50 m from comes again near it
help.sv-join:--spawn-tera: Tera Type, 0 Normal to 17 Fairy in type order (default %(default)s)
help.sv-join:--spawn-ivs: six IVs 0 to 31 (default each random, as a wild one's)
help.sv-join:--spawn-ability: ability slot, 2 the hidden ability (default 0 or 1 at random, as a wild one's)
help.sv-join:--spawn-legal: with --spawn: spawn only while the host stands in an area where PKHeX accepts that spawn caught, found from the wild Pokemon the host's console shares (it shares them once our player is near: --follow-host)
help.sv-join:--scan-only: report what the console advertises and join nothing
help.sv-join:--session-join: send the Pia Session join request in the retail layout (docs/sv.md, The Session join request): ten protocols with their versions, a four-byte nonce, both location ids, a seven-byte station address and one player record. A mesh join is unicast, so no passive capture shows a retail one
help.sv-join:--send-record: after the seat, send this 1395-byte identity record on 0x81 port 1 (our station stream) as the game's data exchange, retransmitting until the host acknowledges it. A retail joiner sends its own identity here
help.sv-join:--no-clock: do not send the Clone Clock request. A seated joiner sends eighteen zero bytes on 0x77 before anything else and the host answers
help.sv-join:--game-channel: announce our own channel table on 0x7c. A station opens the game's channel by sending the same 31-byte table its peer sends on port 1, an open on port 2, and a mirror of every later table update; the peer sends the game on port 0 only once ours is announced (docs/sv.md)
help.sv-join:--record-set: send this directory's records as our own on 0x81 port 1, in sequence order, in place of --mirror-records. `scratchpad/sv_extract_records.py` writes one from a station's own log, so a whole real identity can be replayed rather than the host's mirrored back; by default the recorded set in pokeldn.sv.reference
help.sv-join:--trainer-name: the player name record 1 of our identity carries, the one the trade screen shows
help.sv-join:--no-identity: send no station identity unless --record-set or --send-on-open names one; by default the recorded one in pokeldn.sv.reference
help.sv-join:--mirror-records: send every record the host puts on 0x81 port 0 back on port 1 as our own, in order. A retail joiner answers the host's records with a set of its own; this fills that set with records the game itself composed
help.sv-join:--record-delay: seconds after the seat before the first identity record goes out
help.sv-join:--no-channel-ack: do not acknowledge the host's messages on the game's reliable channel 0x7c
help.sv-join:--port2-now: send the game's type-3 join on 0x7c port 2 with the channel table, rather than in answer to the console's type-7 announcement on 0x80 port 2. A pair's joiner answers the announcement (docs/sv.md, Port 2)
help.sv-join:--send-on-open: DELAY:PROTO:PORT:HEX[:z][:start|:end], sent that many seconds after the host announces key 0x80 open on 0x7c port 1. A station's identity is four messages on 0x7c port 0, the two fragments twice, and nothing sent on that port before the announcement reaches the game; repeatable; by default the identity fragments in pokeldn.sv.reference
help.sv-join:--fresh-pid: offer each record under a new PID and encryption constant, shiny state kept, so a save that took it before takes it again
help.sv-join:--trade-offer: a file holding the 348-byte record this joiner offers (raw, or hex text; a 352-byte game message is stripped of its header). With it the joiner answers the host's offer with its own, confirms, commits, and echoes the four exchange steps the way a pair's joiner does (pokeldn.sv.trade). Repeatable: the second and later records are offered in the same seat, one per trade, as each trade closes
help.sv-join:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
help.sv-join:--offer-set: a field written into the offered record before it is sealed, by its pokeldn.sv.pokemon name: nickname=SHINY, species=906, ivs=31,31,31,31,31,31, trainer_id=12345, ball=4. Repeatable, and `shiny` alone rolls a personality value shiny against the record's own ids
help.sv-join:--offer-dump: write the offered record's 348-byte body to this file as hex and exit, which needs no radio
help.sv-join:--offer-out: a file to write the host's own offer to, the 348-byte body of its 80 00 02 00 message, as hex text
help.sv-join:--offer-after-open: seconds after the host's key-0x80 open at which the joiner offers first, before the host does; without it the joiner answers the host's offer
help.sv-join:--confirm-delay: seconds after the host's confirmation before the joiner's own
help.sv-join:--commit-delay: seconds after the host's confirmation before the joiner commits; the pair's joiner committed 1.5 s after its own confirmation and its host answered in kind
help.sv-join:--quiet-seat: end a seat on which the console has sent nothing at all for this many seconds, and go back to scanning. An association taken outside the console's host phase carries no traffic; without this the run holds it for the whole --hold
help.sv-join:--leave-on-migration: end the seat this many seconds after the console asks us to take the host role (Session type 7), and go back to scanning. A console that sent it sent nothing but NetStartHostMigration afterwards in the seats measured; without this the run holds the seat for the whole --hold
help.sv-join:--stay-on-host-migration: hold the seat after the console's NetStartHostMigration (Net 0x40). By default the joiner leaves on the first one: the console is destroying its network and resends it until every client has left, for up to 4 s
help.sv-join:--announce-timeout: end a seat whose console has not announced on 0x80 port 2 this many seconds after the seat, and go back to scanning. A seat can carry every stream to completion and never be announced (docs/sv.md, Unresolved); board seats that traded announced at 5.8 and 7.7 s
help.sv-join:--no-take-host: when the console hands us the host role before the announcement (not a player leaving), leave its network and become the host with bin/sv_host.py on the same channel and code, as bin/pla_join.py does; needs --answer-migration
help.sv-join:--answer-migration: answer the host's type-7 leave-with-host-migration with a type-8 ack, telling it we accept the host role it is handing over
help.sv-join:--no-update-ack: do not answer a Session type-5 station update with the type 6
help.sv-join:--join-delay: hold the Session join request this long after the seat. A console whose WaitMember (3 to 4 s) ends unjoined leaves with host migration, so a join accepted in its leave wait draws the type 7 (docs/sv.md, What decides a seat)
help.sv-join:--join-repeat: with --session-join, re-send it every N seconds (0 sends it once)
help.sv-join:--join-player-id: the 16-byte player id in the join request: 'arceus' (1 then 0 as two big-endian u64, what a retail Arceus states), 'random', 'high' (random with a leading 0xff) or 32 hex digits. A Scarlet host's own is 10047bd4a25543e057cee5c71ab1f2a2 (sv18)
help.sv-join:--join-player-name: the player name in the join request's one player record; a retail console's is a single space
help.sv-join:--join-flags: message flags on the join request; a joining Arceus sends 0x01, skip the source check, on every repeat of it
help.sv-join:--join-dst-var: the packet header's destination variable id on the join request: 0, which is what a joining Arceus uses, or the host's own
help.sv-join:--net-ack: answer the host's Net 0x11 with the 0x12 ack. A retail joiner does not, and the ack makes the console ask for host migration instead (sv08)
help.sv-join:--connect-timeout: seconds to allow the association itself; a console whose host phase ends mid-connect leaves ldn.connect blocked with no timeout of its own
help.sv-join:--open-delay: seconds after the join response (after the seat without --session-join) before the eleven acks and the two stream opens go out; a retail joiner opens 0.75 s after its join
help.sv-join:--rtt-period: seconds between our own RTT requests (0 sends none)
help.sv-join:--rtt-delay: answer each RTT request SECONDS late; RTT samples enable the host's retransmission timer (docs/sv.md)
help.sv-join:--repeat-ack-gap: acknowledge a record already held at most once per SECONDS per stream; a new record is acked at once. 0 acks every repeat (docs/sv.md)
help.sv-join:--ack-highest: ack one past the highest id received, with no mask, instead of the contiguous run and a mask as a retail station does (docs/sv.md)
help.sv-join:--ack-flags: the Pia message flags on our bulk acks; 0xa0 is what both retail stations send, and bit 5 compresses the message body
help.sv-join:--ack-entries: entries in the ack payload; a retail station sends four
help.sv-join:--ack-dest-bits: the reliable header's destination bits; 3 adds the four-byte bitmap a retail station sends, 0 leaves the nine-byte header
help.sv-join:--ack-sweep: rotate every combination of --ack-flags, --ack-entries and --ack-dest-bits through the seat, one per --ack-sweep-period, and print each as it goes live. One seat then says which shape the guest parses
help.sv-join:--ack-sweep-period: seconds each sweep variant stays live
help.sv-join:--ack-period: seconds between the periodic bulk acks on every stream the host uses
help.sv-join:--unicast: send to the host's address instead of the LDN broadcast address. Both retail stations broadcast every Pia packet (sv11), and a broadcast needs no ARP resolution of the peer
help.sv-join:--verbose-circle: with --union-circle: print each circle message we send and each step of the area search too; the --capture file keeps the steps either way
help.sv-join:--capture: write every datagram here as JSON lines
help.sv-online:--online: trade with a player far away: their console's offer is offered here, and each side confirms only once both consoles have (docs/online.md)
help.sv-online:--online-code: the room both players enter; default the link code, and no code meets anyone else trading online without one
help.sv-online:--capture: write every datagram here as JSON lines
help.sv-online:--violet: advertise Violet's local communication id instead of Scarlet's
help.sv-online:--scene-id: the LDN scene: 4 for a Link Trade, 7 for a Tera Raid
help.sv-online:--max-participants: the LDN participant limit; a Tera Raid advertises 4
help.sv-online:--platform: the station platform byte: 1 is a Switch 2, which is what both retail consoles advertise; 0 is a Switch and what the LDN layer defaults to
help.sv-online:--ssid: hex, 16 bytes; default lets the LDN layer pick
help.sv-online:--ip-host: host over ldn_mitm on the LAN for an emulator; no radio and no root
help.sv-online:--no-leave-response: leave a console's Session type-3 leave request unanswered; it then resends it every 0.5 s and leaves after the fourth (docs/sv.md, Leaving)
help.sv-online:--print-packets: print every packet in and out; the --capture file keeps them either way
help.sv-online:--ack-period: seconds between the periodic bulk acks on every port the console used
help.sv-online:--clock: answer clone clock requests, if any
help.sv-online:--update-seq: the sequence id in the station-list update; a Scarlet host sends 1 where its join response sent 0
help.sv-online:--update-first-seq: also send a station list in the same breath as the join response, under this sequence id; an emulated Scarlet host sends one with id 0 there and the second about two seconds later
help.sv-online:--update-delay: seconds between the Session join response and the station-list update; a Scarlet host leaves about 1.5 s
help.sv-online:--session-flags: the message flags on the Session replies; a Scarlet host sends 0x00, this host's own default is 0x01
help.sv-online:--session-packet-id: the packet id in the Pia header of the Session replies; a Scarlet host's join response carries 1
help.sv-online:--scarlet-response: the 41-byte Session join response a Scarlet host sends, with no route bytes, rather than Arceus's 43-byte one
help.sv-online:--net-flags: the message flags on the Net 0x11 opening; a retail host sends 0x31, this host's own default is 0x01
help.sv-online:--rtt-probe: send an RTT request this often, as a pair's host does every 410 ms; the host otherwise only answers them
help.sv-online:--net-property-flags: the message flags on the Net 0x50; a pair's host sends 0x31 on it and on its 0x11, and this host's 0x11 needs 0x01 to be answered at all
help.sv-online:--net-property: send the Net 0x50 update-property message a pair's host sends 0.37 s after its 0x11, retransmitting until the console's 0x51
help.sv-online:--net-stations: how many 21-byte station slots the Net 0x11 carries; a retail host writes four whatever the game's participant limit is
help.sv-online:--code: the Link Code the player sets, e.g. 12345678; empty for none
help.sv-online:--game-data: hex, the 40 game bytes of the advertisement; a searching console leaves them zero, a host that a joiner reached carried 648cf4 at +0x21
help.sv-online:--send-at: DELAY:PROTO:PORT:HEX[:z][:start|:end], a reliable data message sent that many seconds after the seat; the sequence follows the port's own. A pair's host sends its 0x7c port 1 table update at nine seconds this way
help.sv-online:--record-set: a directory of NNN.bin records to send on 0x81 port 0 as this host's own identity, the way a pair's host sends its 46; the first carries INITIALIZED and every one is already zlib (scratchpad/sv_extract_records.py writes such a set); by default the recorded set in pokeldn.sv.reference
help.sv-online:--trainer-name: the player name record 1 of our identity carries, the one the trade screen shows
help.sv-online:--no-identity: send no station identity unless --record-set or --send-on-open names one; by default the recorded one in pokeldn.sv.reference
help.sv-online:--record-delay: seconds after the seat before the record set goes out
help.sv-online:--records-per-packet: bundle the record set N to a packet, each after the first with its header inherited, as a retail host's retransmit round does (docs/sv.md)
help.sv-online:--record-spacing: seconds between the record packets; a retail raid host spreads its identity over about 0.13 s
help.sv-online:--announce: run the game's port-2 opening from the station ids instead of a replay: the type-7 announcement on 0x80 port 2 carrying this host's own station id, and a type 9 carrying the console's in answer to its type-3 join on 0x7c port 2 (pokeldn.sv.port2)
help.sv-online:--announce-delay: seconds after the seat before the type 7 goes out; a pair's host sends it at about 2.3
help.sv-online:--fresh-pid: offer each record under a new PID and encryption constant, shiny state kept, so a save that took it before takes it again
help.sv-online:--trade-offer: a file holding the 348-byte record this host offers (raw, or hex text; a 352-byte game message is stripped of its header). With it the host answers the console's offer with its own, confirms, and follows the console through the commit and the four exchange steps the way a pair's host does (pokeldn.sv.trade). Repeatable: the second and later records are offered in the same seat, one per trade, as each trade closes
help.sv-online:--gift-event: the Mystery Gift card each --trade-offer was made from, in the same order: its key in PKHeX's event database (pokeldn.pokemon.Service.gift_events)
help.sv-online:--for-receiver: make each --gift-event card that gives the receiver's own trainer again for the console's save, during the trade: the console offers first, a Pokemon its save caught names the trainer, and ours goes up made for it; for any other, the trainer the console's session data names. Failing both, the offer goes as given, under the trainer from Settings (pokeldn.receiver_gift, docs/gift_simulated.md)
help.sv-online:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
help.sv-online:--offer-set: a field written into the offered record before it is sealed, by its pokeldn.sv.pokemon name: nickname=SHINY, species=906, level=50, ivs=31,31,31,31,31,31, pid=0x1234, trainer_id=12345, ball=4, moves=33,0,0,0. Repeatable, and `shiny` alone rolls a personality value shiny against the record's own ids
help.sv-online:--offer-dump: write the offered record's 348-byte body to this file as hex and exit, which needs no radio
help.sv-online:--offer-out: a file to write the console's own offer to, the 348-byte body of its 80 00 02 00 message, as hex text. What it holds is read by pokeldn.sv.pokemon
help.sv-online:--send-on-open: DELAY:PROTO:PORT:HEX[:z][:start|:end], sent that many seconds after the console announces its own key 0x80 open on 0x7c port 1. A port-0 message sent before that open is acknowledged by the console and never reaches the game, and so is everything after it on that port; repeatable; by default the identity fragments in pokeldn.sv.reference
help.sv-online:--offer-after-open: seconds after the console's key-0x80 open at which the host offers first; the same gate as --send-on-open
help.sv-online:--offer-at: seconds after the seat at which the host offers first, before the console does, as a pair's host did; without it the host answers the console's offer
help.sv-online:--confirm-delay: seconds after the console's offer before the host's confirmation
help.sv-online:--raid-seed: host a Tera Raid: the raid seed, eight hex digits; the boss, its Tera type and the rewards follow from it and the four --raid-* context flags
help.sv-online:--raid-pokemon: the party record our player brings to the raid, legal per PKHeX; with --raid-seed
help.sv-online:--raid-reward: a reward row in place of the seed's, in order; up to 45
help.sv-online:--raid-progress: the story stage, which sets a standard crystal's star odds
help.sv-online:--raid-content: a standard or a black (six-star) crystal
help.sv-online:--raid-event: host an event raid: a Poke Portal News delivery's folder (an EventsGallery event, or its Files); the seed draws from the event's encounters at --raid-version and --raid-progress, and --raid-map and --raid-content are unused
help.sv-online:--raid-event-group: the delivery group of the event's den, 1 to 10; by default the first with dens and an encounter at that progress
help.sv-online:--raid-catch-normal: with --raid-event: serve a catch-once encounter (every seven-star raid, Walking Wake, Iron Leaves...) as a normal catch, its capture rate normal and its record number a stand-in no save has caught, so a save that caught it may catch it again; one that cannot be caught stays so (docs/sv_raid.md, Event raids)
help.sv-online:--raid-players: consoles the raid waits for, 1 to 3; it starts once N are in the lobby and every one is Ready, or when the lobby timer runs out
help.sv-online:--raid-partner: an NPC partner the raid seats, in slot order, one per slot the consoles leave empty (2 with one console, 1 with two, none with three): Austin, Ava, Logan, Hailey, Evan, Charlotte, Kylie, Hunter, Gianna, Eli, Henry, Chase, Claire, Brooklyn, Zoe, Samantha, Dylan, Luke; the host draws a partner seed that seats them, the rest drawn freely (docs/sv_raid.md, Partners)
help.sv-online:--raid-partner-progress: the unlock stage the partners come from, which sets their pool, their level being four fifths of --raid-pokemon's; by default --raid-progress's, six stars for a black crystal or a seven-star event raid
help.sv-online:--raid-serve: serve the raid battle from this station with a plugin's battle server (NAME, or the first one loaded): the console and our Pokemon fight one battle; one console only; a failure hands the network over as without it (docs/sv_raid.md, Serving the battle)
