help.sv-circle-join:--spawn: with --union-circle: 10 s after the circle's start demo has ended, keep 3 wild Pokemon of this species (dev number) out 15 to 25 m from the host's player, as a console shares its own: one the host battles, removes or goes more than 50 m from comes again near it
help.sv-circle-join:--spawn-tera: Tera Type, 0 Normal to 17 Fairy in type order (default %(default)s)
help.sv-circle-join:--spawn-ivs: six IVs 0 to 31 (default each random, as a wild one's)
help.sv-circle-join:--spawn-ability: ability slot, 2 the hidden ability (default 0 or 1 at random, as a wild one's)
help.sv-circle-join:--spawn-legal: with --spawn: spawn only while the host stands in an area where PKHeX accepts that spawn caught, found from the wild Pokemon the host's console shares (it shares them once our player is near: --follow-host)
help.sv-circle-join:--scan-only: report what the console advertises and join nothing
help.sv-circle-join:--session-join: send the Pia Session join request in the retail layout (docs/sv.md, The Session join request): ten protocols with their versions, a four-byte nonce, both location ids, a seven-byte station address and one player record. A mesh join is unicast, so no passive capture shows a retail one
help.sv-circle-join:--send-record: after the seat, send this 1395-byte identity record on 0x81 port 1 (our station stream) as the game's data exchange, retransmitting until the host acknowledges it. A retail joiner sends its own identity here
help.sv-circle-join:--no-clock: do not send the Clone Clock request. A seated joiner sends eighteen zero bytes on 0x77 before anything else and the host answers
help.sv-circle-join:--game-channel: announce our own channel table on 0x7c. A station opens the game's channel by sending the same 31-byte table its peer sends on port 1, an open on port 2, and a mirror of every later table update; the peer sends the game on port 0 only once ours is announced (docs/sv.md)
help.sv-circle-join:--record-set: send this directory's records as our own on 0x81 port 1, in sequence order, in place of --mirror-records. `scratchpad/sv_extract_records.py` writes one from a station's own log, so a whole real identity can be replayed rather than the host's mirrored back; by default the recorded set in pokeldn.sv.reference
help.sv-circle-join:--trainer-name: the player name record 1 of our identity carries, the one the trade screen shows
help.sv-circle-join:--no-identity: send no station identity unless --record-set or --send-on-open names one; by default the recorded one in pokeldn.sv.reference
help.sv-circle-join:--mirror-records: send every record the host puts on 0x81 port 0 back on port 1 as our own, in order. A retail joiner answers the host's records with a set of its own; this fills that set with records the game itself composed
help.sv-circle-join:--record-delay: seconds after the seat before the first identity record goes out
help.sv-circle-join:--no-channel-ack: do not acknowledge the host's messages on the game's reliable channel 0x7c
help.sv-circle-join:--port2-now: send the game's type-3 join on 0x7c port 2 with the channel table, rather than in answer to the console's type-7 announcement on 0x80 port 2. A pair's joiner answers the announcement (docs/sv.md, Port 2)
help.sv-circle-join:--send-on-open: DELAY:PROTO:PORT:HEX[:z][:start|:end], sent that many seconds after the host announces key 0x80 open on 0x7c port 1. A station's identity is four messages on 0x7c port 0, the two fragments twice, and nothing sent on that port before the announcement reaches the game; repeatable; by default the identity fragments in pokeldn.sv.reference
help.sv-circle-join:--fresh-pid: offer each record under a new PID and encryption constant, shiny state kept, so a save that took it before takes it again
help.sv-circle-join:--trade-offer: a file holding the 348-byte record this joiner offers (raw, or hex text; a 352-byte game message is stripped of its header). With it the joiner answers the host's offer with its own, confirms, commits, and echoes the four exchange steps the way a pair's joiner does (pokeldn.sv.trade). Repeatable: the second and later records are offered in the same seat, one per trade, as each trade closes
help.sv-circle-join:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
help.sv-circle-join:--offer-set: a field written into the offered record before it is sealed, by its pokeldn.sv.pokemon name: nickname=SHINY, species=906, ivs=31,31,31,31,31,31, trainer_id=12345, ball=4. Repeatable, and `shiny` alone rolls a personality value shiny against the record's own ids
help.sv-circle-join:--offer-dump: write the offered record's 348-byte body to this file as hex and exit, which needs no radio
help.sv-circle-join:--offer-out: a file to write the host's own offer to, the 348-byte body of its 80 00 02 00 message, as hex text
help.sv-circle-join:--offer-after-open: seconds after the host's key-0x80 open at which the joiner offers first, before the host does; without it the joiner answers the host's offer
help.sv-circle-join:--confirm-delay: seconds after the host's confirmation before the joiner's own
help.sv-circle-join:--commit-delay: seconds after the host's confirmation before the joiner commits; the pair's joiner committed 1.5 s after its own confirmation and its host answered in kind
help.sv-circle-join:--quiet-seat: end a seat on which the console has sent nothing at all for this many seconds, and go back to scanning. An association taken outside the console's host phase carries no traffic; without this the run holds it for the whole --hold
help.sv-circle-join:--leave-on-migration: end the seat this many seconds after the console asks us to take the host role (Session type 7), and go back to scanning. A console that sent it sent nothing but NetStartHostMigration afterwards in the seats measured; without this the run holds the seat for the whole --hold
help.sv-circle-join:--stay-on-host-migration: hold the seat after the console's NetStartHostMigration (Net 0x40). By default the joiner leaves on the first one: the console is destroying its network and resends it until every client has left, for up to 4 s
help.sv-circle-join:--announce-timeout: end a seat whose console has not announced on 0x80 port 2 this many seconds after the seat, and go back to scanning. A seat can carry every stream to completion and never be announced (docs/sv.md, Unresolved); board seats that traded announced at 5.8 and 7.7 s
help.sv-circle-join:--no-take-host: when the console hands us the host role before the announcement (not a player leaving), leave its network and become the host with bin/sv_host.py on the same channel and code, as bin/pla_join.py does; needs --answer-migration
help.sv-circle-join:--answer-migration: answer the host's type-7 leave-with-host-migration with a type-8 ack, telling it we accept the host role it is handing over
help.sv-circle-join:--no-update-ack: do not answer a Session type-5 station update with the type 6
help.sv-circle-join:--join-delay: hold the Session join request this long after the seat. A console whose WaitMember (3 to 4 s) ends unjoined leaves with host migration, so a join accepted in its leave wait draws the type 7 (docs/sv.md, What decides a seat)
help.sv-circle-join:--join-repeat: with --session-join, re-send it every N seconds (0 sends it once)
help.sv-circle-join:--join-player-id: the 16-byte player id in the join request: 'arceus' (1 then 0 as two big-endian u64, what a retail Arceus states), 'random', 'high' (random with a leading 0xff) or 32 hex digits. A Scarlet host's own is 10047bd4a25543e057cee5c71ab1f2a2 (sv18)
help.sv-circle-join:--join-player-name: the player name in the join request's one player record; a retail console's is a single space
help.sv-circle-join:--join-flags: message flags on the join request; a joining Arceus sends 0x01, skip the source check, on every repeat of it
help.sv-circle-join:--join-dst-var: the packet header's destination variable id on the join request: 0, which is what a joining Arceus uses, or the host's own
help.sv-circle-join:--net-ack: answer the host's Net 0x11 with the 0x12 ack. A retail joiner does not, and the ack makes the console ask for host migration instead (sv08)
help.sv-circle-join:--connect-timeout: seconds to allow the association itself; a console whose host phase ends mid-connect leaves ldn.connect blocked with no timeout of its own
help.sv-circle-join:--open-delay: seconds after the join response (after the seat without --session-join) before the eleven acks and the two stream opens go out; a retail joiner opens 0.75 s after its join
help.sv-circle-join:--rtt-period: seconds between our own RTT requests (0 sends none)
help.sv-circle-join:--rtt-delay: answer each RTT request SECONDS late; RTT samples enable the host's retransmission timer (docs/sv.md)
help.sv-circle-join:--repeat-ack-gap: acknowledge a record already held at most once per SECONDS per stream; a new record is acked at once. 0 acks every repeat (docs/sv.md)
help.sv-circle-join:--ack-highest: ack one past the highest id received, with no mask, instead of the contiguous run and a mask as a retail station does (docs/sv.md)
help.sv-circle-join:--ack-flags: the Pia message flags on our bulk acks; 0xa0 is what both retail stations send, and bit 5 compresses the message body
help.sv-circle-join:--ack-entries: entries in the ack payload; a retail station sends four
help.sv-circle-join:--ack-dest-bits: the reliable header's destination bits; 3 adds the four-byte bitmap a retail station sends, 0 leaves the nine-byte header
help.sv-circle-join:--ack-sweep: rotate every combination of --ack-flags, --ack-entries and --ack-dest-bits through the seat, one per --ack-sweep-period, and print each as it goes live. One seat then says which shape the guest parses
help.sv-circle-join:--ack-sweep-period: seconds each sweep variant stays live
help.sv-circle-join:--ack-period: seconds between the periodic bulk acks on every stream the host uses
help.sv-circle-join:--unicast: send to the host's address instead of the LDN broadcast address. Both retail stations broadcast every Pia packet (sv11), and a broadcast needs no ARP resolution of the peer
help.sv-circle-join:--verbose-circle: with --union-circle: print each circle message we send and each step of the area search too; the --capture file keeps the steps either way
help.sv-circle-join:--capture: write every datagram here as JSON lines
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--print-packet: print every packet in and out; the --capture file keeps them either way
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--code: join only a console searching with this Link Code; empty takes any
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--comm-id: local communication id to join, hex; default is either cartridge's
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--ip-join: join an emulated console over the LAN through ldn_mitm instead of the radio: no root, no phy, no prod.keys
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--scan-timeout: --ip-join: seconds to wait for one ldn_mitm scan answer
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--dwell: seconds per channel in the scan; the console's hosting window is a few seconds, so a long dwell misses it
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--hold: how long to stay in one joined session before scanning again
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--name: the LDN node name we publish
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--platform: the station platform byte we publish; 1 is what a Switch 2 sends
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--mac: set the adapter's MAC before associating, e.g. 48:f1:eb:11:22:33. Pia derives a station's constant id from its MAC, and the two consoles' are Nintendo OUIs where the adapter's is not. The driver reload in the launcher puts the adapter's own address back
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--scene-id: join only a network of this LDN scene: 4 a Link Trade, 7 a Tera Raid
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--raid-pokemon: join the Tera Raid lobby a console hosts and bring this party record, legal per PKHeX; our player readies, answers the start and leaves when the battle begins, its Pokemon fighting on for the console
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--raid-ready-d: seconds in the raid lobby before our player readies
help.sv-circle-encounters-join:--union-circle: join the Union Circle a console hosts, as a raid guest joins a raid: take the seat, send our identity, open the game's channel, answer the host's start, put our player on the field where the host's stands and hold it for --hold (docs/sv_union_circle.md)

help.za-host:--channel: a searching console put both of its measured sessions on channel 6
help.za-host:--code: the link code the player types
help.za-host:--capture: every datagram as one JSON line
help.za-host:--player-name: the LDN node name; a searching console advertises one space
help.za-host:--trainer-name: the player name our identity carries, the one the trade screen shows
help.za-host:--game-dir: where identity10.bin, identity11b.bin and selection.bin live; by default the ones pokeldn.za.reference ships
help.za-host:--trade-offer: the 354-byte offer message: the preview, then our pick. Repeatable, one per trade in the seat; the last serves every later trade
help.za-host:--fresh-pid: send the offer under a new PID and encryption constant, shiny state kept, so a save that took this record before takes it again
help.za-host:--offer-at: make our pick this many seconds after the preview, without waiting for the console's; the default answers the console's pick
help.za-host:--offer-out: write the Pokemon the console picks here; trade N > 1 writes FILE-N. A preview, the console's cursor on its box, is not written
help.za-host:--ip-host: host an emulated console over ldn_mitm, with no radio
help.za-host:--comm-id: hex; the default is the title's. An emulated Z-A advertises and scans for ffffffffffffffff over ldn_mitm
help.za-host:--hold-after-trade: optional seconds to keep the seat once the console is back on its box after a trade, then hand the console the session and close; by default the host waits for the console to leave
help.za-host:--online: trade with a player far away: their console's offer is offered here, and each side confirms only once both consoles have (docs/online.md)
help.za-host:--online-code: the room both players enter; default the link code, and no code meets anyone else trading online without one
help.za-host:--gift-event: the Mystery Gift card each --trade-offer was made from, in the same order: its key in PKHeX's event database (pokeldn.pokemon.Service.gift_events)
help.za-host:--for-receiver: make each --gift-event card that gives the receiver's own trainer again for the console's save, during the trade: the console offers first, a Pokemon its save caught names the trainer, and ours goes up made for it; for any other, the trainer the console's session data names. Failing both, the offer goes as given, under the trainer from Settings (pokeldn.receiver_gift, docs/gift_simulated.md)
help.za-host:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
help.za-join:--print-packets: print every packet in and out; the --capture file keeps them either way
help.za-join:--dwell: seconds per channel in a scan
help.za-join:--hold: how long to hold one seat
help.za-join:--hold-after-trade: leave this long after the last queued trade's fourth step; by default the seat is kept until the player backs out or --hold ends, as every joiner does
help.za-join:--quiet-seat: end a seat on which the console has sent nothing for this long
help.za-join:--connect-timeout: bound the association alone; the seat itself is not bounded by it
help.za-join:--platform: the station platform byte; both retail consoles here are Switch 2
help.za-join:--mac: give the phy this MAC before associating
help.za-join:--comm-id: hex; the default is Legends Z-A's
help.za-join:--code: only join a console waiting on this link code
help.za-join:--capture: every datagram as one JSON line
help.za-join:--net-probe: send the band's Net connection request once seated
help.za-join:--no-answer: stay silent; the run then measures what the console sends on its own
help.za-join:--withhold: never send this answer, to find what a seat needs (docs/za.md, Unresolved); repeatable
help.za-join:--session-join: send the Session join request once the console's Net is acknowledged
help.za-join:--join-repeat: V-Blank ticks between re-sends of an unanswered Session join; 0 is once
help.za-join:--app-ver: hex; the application communication version the Session join declares. Six is what a reference joiner sends and what the advertisement carries
help.za-join:--token: hex; the Session join's 32-byte identification token, zero-padded. A reference joiner sends 0x06 and zeroes
help.za-join:--player-name: the name the Session join's PlayerInfo carries; a reference joiner sends one space
help.za-join:--trainer-name: the player name our identity carries, the one the trade screen shows
help.za-join:--source-id: our own constant id in the Session join: the LDN permutation of our MAC, which is the form the console publishes for itself, or the MAC as it is
help.za-join:--protocols: id:version pairs the Session join declares; the default is the set a reference Legends Z-A joiner declares
help.za-join:--join-flags: hex packet flags ORed into the Session join's header: 4 is the band's skip-network-connection-check bit, which a station the console has not yet connected may owe
help.za-join:--game: once the session is up, open the game's reliable streams and send the identity, the selection record and, with --trade-offer, an offer
help.za-join:--game-dir: where the reference payloads (identity10.bin, selection.bin, ...) live; by default the ones pokeldn.za.reference ships
help.za-join:--fresh-pid: send the offer under a new PID and encryption constant, shiny state kept, so a save that took this record before takes it again
help.za-join:--offer-out: write the host's offered PA9 here; trade N > 1 writes FILE-N
help.za-join:--trade-offer: a 354-byte offer message to send once the streams are open. Repeatable, one per trade in the seat; the last serves every later trade
help.za-join:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
help.za-join:--selection-delay: seconds after the identity before the selection record starts; a reference joiner waits about 0.46 s
help.za-join:--selection-period: seconds between selection records; a reference joiner sends about four a second, each under a fresh sequence
help.za-join:--selection-count: how many selection records to send; a reference joiner sent sixteen
help.za-join:--offer-delay: seconds after the streams open before the offer goes out
help.za-join:--ip-join: join an emulated host over the LAN through its ldn_mitm bridge, with no radio and no root
help.za-join:--our-ip: our own address on that LAN
help.za-join:--seat-marker: a file to write the moment a seat forms and again when it ends, so a watcher on the other side can act on the seat without a relay
help.za-join:--node-version: the local communication version our NodeInfo publishes on the LAN path; a host publishes its own application version there
help.za-join:--broadcast: address our datagrams to the link-local broadcast, as a retail station does
help.za-join:--our-var: the variable id we send as our own until the console names one
help.za-join:--unicast: address our datagrams to the host rather than to the broadcast
help.za-online:--channel: a searching console put both of its measured sessions on channel 6
help.za-online:--code: the link code the player types
help.za-online:--capture: every datagram as one JSON line
help.za-online:--player-name: the LDN node name; a searching console advertises one space
help.za-online:--trainer-name: the player name our identity carries, the one the trade screen shows
help.za-online:--game-dir: where identity10.bin, identity11b.bin and selection.bin live; by default the ones pokeldn.za.reference ships
help.za-online:--trade-offer: the 354-byte offer message: the preview, then our pick. Repeatable, one per trade in the seat; the last serves every later trade
help.za-online:--fresh-pid: send the offer under a new PID and encryption constant, shiny state kept, so a save that took this record before takes it again
help.za-online:--offer-at: make our pick this many seconds after the preview, without waiting for the console's; the default answers the console's pick
help.za-online:--offer-out: write the Pokemon the console picks here; trade N > 1 writes FILE-N. A preview, the console's cursor on its box, is not written
help.za-online:--ip-host: host an emulated console over ldn_mitm, with no radio
help.za-online:--comm-id: hex; the default is the title's. An emulated Z-A advertises and scans for ffffffffffffffff over ldn_mitm
help.za-online:--hold-after-trade: optional seconds to keep the seat once the console is back on its box after a trade, then hand the console the session and close; by default the host waits for the console to leave
help.za-online:--online: trade with a player far away: their console's offer is offered here, and each side confirms only once both consoles have (docs/online.md)
help.za-online:--online-code: the room both players enter; default the link code, and no code meets anyone else trading online without one
help.za-online:--gift-event: the Mystery Gift card each --trade-offer was made from, in the same order: its key in PKHeX's event database (pokeldn.pokemon.Service.gift_events)
help.za-online:--for-receiver: make each --gift-event card that gives the receiver's own trainer again for the console's save, during the trade: the console offers first, a Pokemon its save caught names the trainer, and ours goes up made for it; for any other, the trainer the console's session data names. Failing both, the offer goes as given, under the trainer from Settings (pokeldn.receiver_gift, docs/gift_simulated.md)
help.za-online:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
